Patindogí (walâ níya pagapatindogí, walâ níya pagpatindogí) sing baláy iníng lugár. Build (he is not building, has not built) a house on this pot.

The letter "i" is pronounced in Visayan as in Spanish, except when it has an abrupt sound as in the words:-dalî, dalîdálì, tahî, hibî, etc. To avoid an hiatus "i" slurs into a following vowel as if a "y" had been inserted, and in fact "y" is often inserted in modern spelling, e.g. hiás, hiyás, tián, tiyán; íos, íyos, etc. However a distinct hiatus occurs when an abrupt "i" is followed by a vowel, e.g. daliá, dali-á, not dalyá; tahión, tahi-ón, not tahiyón; ginharían, ginharí-an, not ginharíyan, etc. (From dalî, tahî, hárì, etc.).

His, etc. See íya, ána. (see ákon).
His, etc. See íya, ána. (see ákon).
To squawk, squeal, etc. See iyágak, íyak.
To squawk, squeal, etc. See iyágak, íyak.
A grain (separated from the ear), a shelled pea or bean, or the like. Madámù ang mga iás sa ímo tabíg. There are many loose rice-grains in your harvesting basket. (see iyás, uyás, lamígas).
A grain (separated from the ear), a shelled pea or bean, or the like. Madámù ang mga iás sa ímo tabíg. There are many loose rice-grains in your harvesting basket. (see iyás, uyás, lamígas).

(B) Company, companion, chum, pal, friend; to accompany, go with, go along with, keep-, bear-, company. Sín-o ang ibá mo? May ibá ikáw? Who is your companion? Have you a companion? Sín-o ang ibá mo kahápon? Sín-o ang nagibá sa ímo kahápon? Who was with you yesterday? Ibahí akó pakádto sa Ilóngílong. Come along with me to Iloilo. Ibahán ko siá. I shall keep him company. Ibahón ko siá. I shall have him as my companion. (see upúd, búylog, tawás).

(B) Company, companion, chum, pal, friend; to accompany, go with, go along with, keep-, bear-, company. Sín-o ang ibá mo? May ibá ikáw? Who is your companion? Have you a companion? Sín-o ang ibá mo kahápon? Sín-o ang nagibá sa ímo kahápon? Who was with you yesterday? Ibahí akó pakádto sa Ilóngílong. Come along with me to Iloilo. Ibahán ko siá. I shall keep him company. Ibahón ko siá. I shall have him as my companion. (see upúd, búylog, tawás).

The soft Visayan aspirate is best represented by the letter "H" pronounced as in English. Therefore the letter "J" can be dispensed with in writing Visayan, even when Spanish words occur, such as:-Jesucristo, José, alhajas, etc., which are spelled:-Hesukrísto, Hosé, aláhas, etc.

This letter has the same sound as the English "c" in "cat, come, cut, fact, etc.", but is pronounced a little softer than "ck" in "lack, pack, struck, etc.". Modern writers almost exclusively employ "k", where formerly "c" (before "a", "o", "u", all consonants and hyphens, and at the end of words) and "qu" (before "e" and "i") were used. Bearing this in mind it is easy to find in this dictionary expressions originally written according to the old spelling, as acó, caácò, catacá, cácac, bác-hò, bác-it, báquid, quíquic, etc., under akó, kaákò, kataká, kákak, bákhò, bák-it, bákid, kíkik, etc.  The prefixes pan-, hi-, ha-, etc., if composed with words beginning with the letter "k", become pang-, hing-, hang-, etc. and the "k" drops out, e.g. karós-pangarós; kaláyo-hingaláyo; kuyús-hanguyús, etc.

(H) Personal pronoun, often used for ikáw-you (singular). Sín-o ka balá? Who are you? Diín ka makádto? Where are you going to? Ginbayáran ka na níya sang íya útang sa ímo? Has he paid you what he owed you?

A particle employed to connect a cardinal or ordinal numeral with a noun or with another numeral. "Ka" is also used after distributives, and after the indefinite "pilá", whenever the latter has the meaning of "how many" or "few", e.g. Duhá ka púlò ka líbo. Twenty thousand. Tátlo ka gatús ka líbo kà táo. Three hundred thousand men. Limá ka karabáw. Five buffaloes. Amó iní ang ikapúlò níla ka anák. This is their tenth child. Sa ikawaló ka (nga) ádlaw sa búlan sa Enéro. On the eighth day of January. Pilá silá ka táo? How many are they? Mga pilá lámang ka táo ang nagtalámbong. Only a few men attended. Nakabáton silá sing tagnapúlò ka mángmang. They received ten pesos each.

A prefix of very wide use in the formation of abstract and collective nouns as well as of an exclamatory superlative which nearly corresponds in meaning to the English "How--!" e.g. álam-kaálam (wisdom, learning); písan-kapísan (diligence, application); píntas-kapíntas (cruelty); ángot-kaangtánan (connection); lábut-kalabtánan (participation, implication); uyáng-kahinguyángan (outlay, expenditure); bátà-kabatáan (childhood; children); baláy-kabalayán (houses, collection of houses); támad-katámad sa ímo! How lazy you are! Dásig-kadásig siníng kabáyo! How swiftly this horse runs! gáhud, galúng-kagáhud kag kagalúng sináng mga bátà! Oh, the noisiness and boisterousness of those children! lisúd-ay, kalisúd! Oh, what a heavy cross! After superlative adverbs like lakás, lám-ag, dúro, masyádo, támà, túman, etc. "ka" is either prefixed to the adjectives or takes the place of ma-, e.g. Dalók-greedy. Lakás kadalók. Very greedy. Layâ-dry. Masyádo kalayâ. Very dry. Maitúm-black. Lám-ag kaitúm. Very black. Madálum-deep. Dúro kadálum. Very deep. Matámbok-fat. Támà katámbok. Very fat. Dakû-large. Túman kadakû. Very large, etc.

In modern Visayan ka-is quite frequently used instead of pagka-in the formation of abstract nouns from "ma-adjectives", e.g. kamatinoóhon (pagkamatinoóhon)-faith, credulity; kamatinahóron (pagkamatinahóron)-respectfulness, and many more.

Notwithstanding that others praise him, I for my part consider him a bad (ugly) man. Indì mo pagkaduón (paglaw-ayón) ang pagsulát. Don't write badly, i.e. illegibly, indistinctly, obscenely. (see láin, láw-ay, hígkò, maláin, maláw-ay, mahígkò, kadô).

Wariness, watchfulness, carefulness, guardedness, caution, alertness, suspicion. Kon may kadudláan na ang mga pumulúyò, salâ inâ sang mga punóan nga nagbúhat sing mga kalaínan sa bánwa. If the people are now cautious (or suspicious) the fault lies with those officials who did harm to the town (the state or commonwealth). (see dúdlà).
Darkness, quality of being dark or obscure. (see dulúm, kadudúlman).
Extreme poverty, misery, wretchedness. (dungúl).
Augmentation, increase, growth, development, addition. (see dúgang).
(H) See kabuháyan.

Blood relationship, consanguinity, condition of belonging to the same stock. Kadúgò silá. They are of the same stock (or family). Ang áton mga kadúgò. Those of our own kin. Our own kith and kin. (dugô; see himatâ, kahimataán, kakilíran, kasimánwa).
Doubt, indecision, hesitation, wavering, misgiving, suspense. Sa walâ sing (sa waláy) kaduháduháan --. Without doubt --. Doubtless --. (see duhádúha).
Darkness, etc. (see kadudúlman, kadulumánan).
See kadudúlman id.
Hatred, grudge, spite, ill-will. (see dumút).
See kadúnut. Also: Things that are rotten, corrupt, decayed, decomposed, putrid, putrified. (see dúnut, dunút).
See kadúnut.
A kind of small mushroom growing mostly on rotten wood, and used for food.
(H) Countries, fields, grounds. (dútà).
See kadúyug. Also: Habits; likings, leanings, instinct.

To grasp or snatch greedily, with out-stretched arm and clawing hand, seize precipitately, catch unceremoniously. Indì ka magkádwas sang súd-an. Indì mo pagkadwasón ang súd-an. Don't snatch at the side-dishes so greedily. (see búklas, ágaw).
A kind of peas. See kadiós.
The conjunctive particle: And. Si nánay kag si tátay. Father and mother. Ang kánding kag ang idô. The goat and the dog. Nagdalágan siá kag dinakúp níya ang makáwat. He ran and caught the thief.
To waste, wear out, grow lean or weak, lose strength or vigour. Nagakág-as siá sa kalisúd. She is wasting away under a load of troubles. (see hágas).
(H) Deep night, night-time.
(B) See kagab-íhon.
See kagabúk. Also: Rotten state of affairs, corruption, graft, etc.

(H) The little (as opposed to the great), the lower classes of people, the poor or uninfluential members of a community; the least or smallest (of a kind). (see gágmay, kadalagkuán-the great, rich or prominent people).
(H) A forceful expression used in anger or passion. Kagalátud (iníng) siníng táo! Curse the man! Damn the man! (gátud).
Weeds, shrubs, brushwood. (see gámhon).
Attraction, allurement, enticement, temptation. (see gányat).
See kagarók. Also: Things that give or cause trouble, etc.

Dry, brittle, friable, fragile; to be or become dry, etc. Iníng mga dáhon sang tabákò nagkagáskas. These tobacco-leaves have become dry or brittle. Ang tabákò mo kagáskas. Your tobacco is dry. (see matískug, matapúk, kagíng, kigás).
Things requiring expenditure; expenditure. (see kagastóhan).

The shears of a lobster, shrimp or the like; to bite, snap, nip, grip, seize with the teeth or with the equivalent of teeth; to catch hold (of inanimate things). Ang mga idô nagakadtánay (for nagakagatánay). The dogs are biting each other. Ang lánsang nagakagát na. The nail has now a firm grip or hold. Ginkagát (kinagát) ang bátà sang báboy. The child was bitten by the pig. Ang ginkádtan (kinádtan) sang idô naghubág. The place bitten by the dog swelled up.
Habits, custom, manner of acting or behaving, behaviour, moral character. (see gáwì, ginawî, batásan, kabatasánan, kabuyó, kinaanáran, kostúmbre).
Full of germs or microbes. (see kágaw).
See kagayón. Also: Things that are beautiful or attractive.

Grief, sorrow, mourning, sadness, desolation, anguish, pain; to grieve, etc. Nagakághà siá. She is grieving. Ginakaghaán níya ang kamatáyon sang íya ilóy. He is mourning the death of his mother. Indì ka magpakághà sa ímo mga ginikánan. Don't sadden your parents. Indì mo pagsóndon ang mga batásan nga maláut nga igkakághà sang ímo mga ginikánan. Don't imitate bad conduct that will grieve your parents. Sa dakû nga kághà kag kasubô --. In great grief and sorrow --. (see subô, lisúd, sákit).
A skin-disease similar to "arikís".
(H) Pertaining to or affected with the skin-disease "kagídkid".
To arrange, order, etc. See kaláging.
Very dry, dried up, hard, brittle, exsiccated, destitute of moisture. (see káging, layâ, layóng, malá, kusúg).
A small branch or twig (of bamboo, etc.). (see símsim, gáwgaw).
Anything that supports life, or that gives relief. Ang swéldo siníng maéstro amó ang kaginhawáan sang íya nga ginikánan. This teacher's salary goes to support his parent. (see ginháwa).
Life, breath, breathing, full liberty to act and enjoy life, independence. (see ginháwa).

Peacefulness, tranquillity, quiet, repose, calmness; joy, pleasure. Walâ sing kagirihim-után ang kalibútan, kon daláyon gid lang magtalibóbò ang ulán. There is no pleasure in life (in the world), when it always rains. Walâ sing kagirihim-után ang íya guyá, panumdúman, etc. He looks worried, his mind is troubled, etc. (see buót, hamúot).
See kagirihim-után.
To scrape with an edged instrument. Kagisí ang kawáyan, káhoy, lamésa, etc. Scrape the bamboo, wood, table, etc. (see kagús, águs, kískis).
Close together, spaced near together. (see íkit).

To penetrate, enter, pierce, affect deeply, touch. Nagakágit inâ sa ákon tagiposóon. That touches me deeply-or-That pierces my heart. Kinagítan ang íya kasíngkásing sináng mga sinúgid. He was touched to the quick by these reports. (see látum, túduk, panalúgsug, panalúpsup).

To ask, request the hand of the bride on behalf of the bridegroom, to woo for, procure a wife for a prospective husband, make a match, be a matchmaker or go-between. Ang tiglalakí nagakágon sa tigbabaé. The father of the man is arranging the marriage with the father of the woman. Kagáb-i ginkagónan si Mariá sang amáy ni Pédro. Last night Peter's father asked for the hand of Maria (on behalf of Peter). Ikágon mo akó ánay sa kay Fulána. Kindly speak for me to N.N. and ask her to become my wife.
A rasp, scraper for the operation of "kágot". (see kalagót).
To scrape, scratch, scoop out with a sharp instrument. Kagóta iní. Scrape this. Kagóti ang kapáyas sing líso. Scoop the pips out of the papaw. (see kódkod).
See kádtan, kádton. (All verbal forms of kagát-to bite).
(H) Jungle, virgin forest.
The eldest brother or sister. (see pangánay, kagurángan, kamagulangán).
Age, oldness. Pilá ka túig ang kagulangón mo? What is your age? How old are you? (see katigulangón-senility, old age).
Hollow, void, empty; brainless, inane, vacuous. (see búngaw, kalóng).

To clean, scrape, scratch with an edged instrument. Kagusá ang lamésa. Scrape the table, (the whole table). Kagusí ang lamésa. Scrape the table, (in places where scraping is needed). Ikágus iníng kotsílyo sa bánkò. Use this knife to scrape the bench with. Kinagusán mo na ang síya? Have you cleaned the chair by scraping it? Have you scraped the chair clean? (see kagís, kískis, águs).
(Sp. caja) Box, safe, case. (see sulúdlan).
See kahádluk. Also: Fearful, dreadful, horrible, frightful; origin of fear, things that inspire terror or apprehension. (see kalahadlukán).
State of being haunted, feeling of fear in a lonely place, ghostliness. (hágnup).
(H) See kahadlukán, kalahadlukán.
Glee, cheer, pleasure, fun; laughable, comic, gleeful, cheerful, cheery, pleasant, funny; motive or cause of complacency, things exciting great fun or laughter. (see hám-ut).
(H) Fear, apprehension, uneasiness; dreadful, fearful, awful; things that are dangerous or that cause uneasiness of mind. (hangáwà).
(H) Remoteness, distance, farness. (see layô).
To touch, feel. (see ipangaláham). The simple káham seems to be out of use.
(H) See kahalam-útan, kaham-útan.
Idle talk, gossip, useless chatting, boasting, bragging. (see hámbug).
Preciousness, costliness, dearness, high value. (see bilí, hamilí).
Position, condition, state, station, circumstances. (butáng; see kabtángan, kahimtángan).
Peacefulness, happiness, prosperity, affluence. (hamungáyà).
An incident, event, happening. (see tabû).
(H) See kahalangáw-an.
Wind; air, atmosphere, climate. (hángin).
Happenings, events, incidents, facts, history. (see hanabû, tabû).
Yesterday (in (during) daytime). Kahápon nga ága. Yesterday morning. Kahápon nga (sing) hápon. Yesterday afternoon or evening.
Yesterday (in (during) daytime). Kahápon nga ága. Yesterday morning. Kahápon nga (sing) hápon. Yesterday afternoon or evening.
Yesterday (in (during) daytime). Kahápon nga ága. Yesterday morning. Kahápon nga (sing) hápon. Yesterday afternoon or evening.
Evening. (see hápon).
See kahapús. Also: things that are easy, the easiest of a kind. Amó iní ang kahapusán sa tanán nga tulún-an. That is the easiest of all the (text) books.

To hazard, dare, venture, be audacious, reckless, intrepid, impertinent, insolent, daring, bold, high-spirited, dauntless. Kinahásan níya ang paghinguyáng sang pílak nga ginpatágò ko sa íya. He dared to spend the money I had entrusted to him for safe keeping. Indì mo pagkahásan ang pagbukás sang ganháan kon walâ ka sing túgut sa pagsulúd. Don't dare to open the door, unless you have permission to enter. (see aháng, ahás).
(H) Slavery, peonage, bondage, peonism, serfdom, villeinage, villenage, complete subjection. (see ulípon).
Desert, waste, wilderness, territory destitute of trees and shrubs; a lonely or isolated place. (see háwà).
See kaháwan. Also: things that are free, unencumbered, unobstructed.
(Sp. cajero) Cashier, treasurer, cash-keeper. (see kúymi, kwími, tesoréro).
Straits, difficulties, want, misery. (hi-ól; see kahil-ánan).
(B) Foot. (see tiíl).
To remove, push or kick off as with the feet. Kahíga sang sílhig ang ití sang manók. Remove the chicken's excrement with the broom.

To scratch with the feet as a chicken. Ang manók nagakáhig sang dútà. The chicken is scratching the ground. Ginakahígan sang manók ang dútà. The ground is being scratched by the chicken. (see pangáhig).
(H) Corners, nooks, out-of-the-way places. (higád; see binít, bá-id, duók, suók, hilít).
Occasion, opportunity.
See kahígkò. Also: depravity, immorality, moral filth, abomination, lechery, lewdness.
(Sp. cajel) A small orange indigenous to the Philippines.
Straits, hardship, weariness, misery. (hi-ól).
See kahilábtan.
Rueful, woeful, piteous, pitiful, objects to be treated tenderly or to be sympathized with. (see hinóklog, hanóklog, makahanóklog).
Tenderness, sympathy, pity, mildness. (see hinóklog, kahinoklógon).
Freedom, independence, liberty. (see kahílway).
Relations, relatives, kindred, kin, kith and kin, kinsfolk, kinship, offspring, progeny. (bátà, himatâ).
Bliss, blessedness, glory, happiness, felicity; blissful, felicitous; objects whose possession gives happiness. (see himáyà).

Deed, action, performance, doings; result, effect, issue, event; possibility of performance. Inâ walâ gid man sing kahimoán. That comes (came) to nothing,-cannot (could not) be done,-is (was) of no effect. (see hímò).
See kahímpit. Also: Perfections, virtues, habits or actions that are perfect or praiseworthy. (see kalantipán).
Position, rank, state, station, condition, circumstances. (butáng; see kabtángan, kahamtángan).
Expenditure, outlay, waste; squandering, extravagance, wastefulness, prodigality. (see uyáng).
See kahinóklog.
See kahi-ól, kahil-ánan.
(H) See kahiolípnan, kahaulipónan.
(Sp. cajeta) A little box; cash-box, jewel-case.
See kahitaásan.
(Sp. cajetilla) Package, box, (as of cigarettes, matches, etc.).
(Sp. cajon) Box, trunk, case; dam, dyke, ditch, bank, particularly applied to banks that inclose rice-fields. Also verb: Kahoní ang ímo talámnan. Put a bank around your field. (see sulúdlan).
Tree; wood.
See kahi-ól id.
Justice, jurisprudence, court of justice. Tiglikúm sang báhin sa kahukmánan. Secretary of Justice. (see hokóm, holokmánan).
See kahil-ánan. (hu-ól-hi-ól; see kalisdánan, kapipít-an, kalalát-an).
Unsteadiness, restlessness, instability, unstableness, fickleness, shakiness, lack of stability or firmness. (see húlag).
Ease, facility. See kahulás.
(H) See kahulúbgon.
(H) Shame, disgrace, disrepute, debasement, degradation, ignominy, humiliation; things or actions that are shameful, disreputable or disgraceful. (huyâ).
Completion, execution, fulfilment, accomplishment. (see humán).
See kahúsay. Also: A clearing up, a settling or adjustment of a dispute, quarrel, debt, etc.
Shame, disgrace, debasement, degradation; remorse mingled with shame. (see kahuyâ, kahulúy-an).
Bent, inclination, leaning. (see húyug, huyúg).
See kaígò. Also: things that are fit, proper or right.
(B) Shame; to be ashamed, etc. See huyâ. Naihâ (nagkaihâ) siá. He was ashamed. Ginkaihaán ko siá. I am ashamed of him. Indì ka maihâ (magkaihâ). Don't be ashamed. Don't be shy or bashful.
Desire, instinct, passion, lust, appetite, prurience, cupidity, concupiscence, especially with regard to carnal emotions. (see íbug).
See kailíbgon id.
Wretched, miserable, poor, pitiable, woeful, unfortunate.
A kind of fruit tree.
See kaímol. Also: Things that make life hard and poor, beggary, pauperism, impecuniousness.
See kaímol. (see kaimolán).
Affability, amiableness, sociableness, sociability. (áblaw; see kaabiabíhon).

Practice and result of jungle-burning, burned clearing, clearing; to burn or fire a piece of grass-land, jungle or mountainside. Nagakaingín silá dídto sa bakólod. They are burning (or firing) the grass there on the hill. Kaíngna (kainginá) iníng talónan. Set fire to this jungle. (see tútud, súnug).
See kaínit. Also: The thick of a fight, heavy work during the heat of the day, etc. (see inítan).
Heat, especially the heat of the sun. See kaínit.
See kaínot. (see kaímot).
China, the Chinese, Chinamen, the Chinese nation. (see ínsik).
(Sp. cairel) Appendage, fringe, silk-band, watch-chain.
See kairél id.

Full, stuffed, crammed, brimful, chockfull, chokefull, bulging; to be or become full, etc. Abáw, balíkda ináng bátà nga nagakâkâ ang íya bólsa sang kamúnsil. My! look back at that boy whose pockets are stuffed with camunsel-fruit. Kâkâ ang íya púyo. His purse is full. (see bát-al, punô, báknal).
Cackle, cackling; to cackle; to talk or shout much. (see kákak).
Forest, wood, coppice, copse; collection of trees, wood, timber, lumber. (see káhoy).
Cackling; to cackle. Ang mungâ nagakákak. The hen cackles. (see kakáak, kurukutúk-to cluck).
Spain; Spaniards; the Spanish Nation. (see Katsílà).
(Sp. cacao) The cacao-tree and its fruit; cocoa.
See kakínot, kaínot. Also: Collective of all things that bring about economy or frugal living.
See kakínot.
(B) Narrowness, tightness, little breadth or width. (see kitíd).
Place where much cogon-grass grows; mountain side or field covered with cogon-grass. (see kógon, kakogonán).
See kakógnan.
(H) Pottery, pots and jars. (see kólon).
A sneak, trickster, cheat; fool; to fool, cheat, trick. Ginakákoy lang níya siá. He is just fooling him. Indì mo akó pagkakóyon. Don't fool, trick or cheat me. (see búang, hásò, lágit, agóng, etc.).
See kakubús. Also: the humble, poor, low caste, low class, Pariah.
Want, need, lack, insufficiency. (see kulábus).
Shortcomings, lack, want, insufficiency. (see kúlang).
(H) See kakúlì. Also: Difficulties, hardships, things requiring hard work or great patience.
(H) Laboriousness, etc. See kakúlì.
A croak, the hoarse, harsh cry of a frog; to croak (as a frog). Ang mga pakâ (pánkà) nagakálà. Frogs croak. N.B. The Dim. and Freq. kalâkalâ is more in use.
(H) A field planted one year which without additional planting yields its produce the following year also, (especially applied to sugar-cane fields). (see dáan).
(H) Cloth to be worked up, or fit to be worked up, into farmers' shirts called "kába".
The greater part or number, majority. (labán; see kadám-an).
(Sp. garbanzo) A kind of chick-peas.
(H) Length. See kalábà.
The larger or greater share, more than others, or more than is left; excess, superfluity, superabundance, redundancy, what is beyond due limits. (see labáw).
(Sp. calavera) Skull. (see bagól).

Preference, preponderance, excellence, privilege, value or esteem set upon one thing rather than another. Ang mga kalabihán sang Mahál nga Bírhen. The excellences or glories of the Blessed Virgin. (see labí).
Eggs to be hatched. (see kalabkában).
Relations, connection, interest, implication, participation, share, interference, meddling. (see lábut, kalabútan).
(B) See kalabaón.
(H) Astonishment, amazement, wonder, surprise; wonderful, astounding, amazing. (búlung). (see kahaurungán).
Prison, gaol. (see kalabóso, karsíl, bilanggóan).
A kind of "dágmay". (see gládì).

(H) Fun, funniness, drollery, ludicrousness, laughableness, ridiculousness, pleasantry, anything that excites laughter (with or without contempt); ridiculous, funny, droll, etc. (see kádlaw, kalaham-után).
(Sp. calado) Draught of a vessel; fretwork. (see dágpak).
(Sp. cuadrado) Square. (see kasílo).
(H) Place to go to or arrive at. (kádto; see kadtoán).
(B) Intelligence, sensibility, sensibleness, sense, reasonableness, judiciousness, understanding, prudence, common sense, wisdom, sagacity, sagaciousness. (see ísip, ihibaló, kalibútan).
Soul, spirit, moral and spiritual nature of man; a disembodied spirit; vitality, moving spirit. (see kálag, láwas-body, matter).
(H) Mourning, grief, sorrow; what is to be mourned over or grieved at, lamentable. (see kághà, makakalágha).

To arrange, dispose, marshal, array, regulate, put in order; prepare well, drill, make ship-shape. Kalagínga ang mga tulún-an, bánkò, láta, botílya, etc. Set in order the books, benches, tins, bottles, etc. Kinalagíngan akó níya sang mga galamitón sang ákon balatonán. He arranged for me the furniture of my reception room. Ginkaláging sang mananábang sing maáyo ang mga sáksi. The lawyer drilled (prepared) the witnesses well. (see káging, húsay, hímos, áman, híwat).
Destruction, perdition, ruin. (see láglag).
Of, or pertaining to, the soul or spirit, spiritual, immaterial. (see kalág, espirituhánon).
(H) A rasp, a kind of coarse file. (see kagót, kágot).

(H) Noise, commotion, stir, excitement, disturbance, riot, sensation; making a stir, causing or exciting a commotion, etc. Kalagulaán iníng mga balítà sa dílì madúgay. These reports will soon cause a sensation. (see makagulúlà, gúlà, gamó).
(H) Things that excite fear or terror; fearsome, fearful, terrible, awful, horrible, dreadful, frightful, alarming, appalling. (see hádluk, kahadlukán).
(H) Merriment, pleasure, pleasantry, fun, mirth, drollery, buffoonery, things that excite laughter and merriment. (see hám-u, kahám-ut, kaham-útan, kaham-utánan, makahalám-ut).
(H) Fear, apprehension, etc. See kahalangáw-an, kahangaláw-an, kahangáwà.

(H) Grief, sorrow, pity, commiseration, sympathy; things that excite pity or compassion, pitiable, woeful, lamentable, sad, distressful, deplorable, pathetic, touching, affecting. (see subô, hanúsbò).
Rake, anything that is used for raking. (see káhig, kahíg).
(H) Things to be-cherished,-desired,-regretted (when lost); desirable, lovely, highly praised or esteemed; regrettable. (see hílak, makahihílak, makahilílak).
Poisonous, venomous, baneful, noisome, noxious. (see hilô, makahihílo, karahílo).
(H) Attraction, attractiveness, fascination, winsomeness, allurement, enticement, charm; attractive, seductive, winning, captivating, charming, fascinating, bewitching. (see ílà, makailílà).
Difference, diversity, variety, unlikeness, dissimilarity.

(H) Jungle or grass to be burned or fired. Siá amó ang tag-* *íya sang madámù nga kalaíngnon. He is the owner of many parcels of land that can be cleared by fire and made fit for the plough. (see kaingín).
Excess, extreme, radicalism, extravagance, intemperance. (lakás).
Men, males, menfolk. (see laláki).
Evils, harm, injury, affliction, disaster, misfortune. (see láut).
(H) A flat-bottomed sieve or low-brimmed basket mainly used to separate freshly pounded rice from the chaff. (see karáraw).
(H) See kalaláwdan.
Road, line, limit, boundary; to lie athwart, lie across, be in the passage of. (see lábang, labangán, kalbangán).
What is to be wound on a bobbin, as a thread, etc. (kalíngyas).
(H) Pleasure, things that give joy or pleasure; pleasant, pleasurable, enjoyable, gratifying. (see lípay, kalípay, makalilípay, malipáyon, malipayón).
(H) Promptness, despatch, expedition, first opportunity; anything that does not suffer delay or should be done quickly. (see kalít).
(H) Pitiableness, anything that excites pity or compassion. (see kalalóy-an, makaloló-oy).
Things to be scratched or dug out, as roots, tubers, etc. (kálot; see talangkónon).
What is to be scratched, rubbed or soothed, as an itch; trial, hardship, difficulty; hard to bear or suffer. (see kálot, kalalóton).
See kalalo-oyán id.
Loveliness, attraction, charm; likeable, lovely, charming, pleasing, captivating, anything that excites a liking, affection or passion for. (see lúyag, makalulúyag, maluyagón, pangaluyág).
Place where digging is done, a mine, or the like. (see káli).
To tickle, itch, irritate, titillate. Ginakalamán akó. I have a tickling feeling.
(H) Novelty, modernity, novel or new-fangled things. (see bág-o, kamág-o, kamag-ohán).
(H) See kalamatáyan id.
A sweet dish of crushed or pulverised rice mixed with sugar and the juice of coconut-meat.
See awóáwo id.
Tripod, especially a small iron one for use in the kitchen.
(H) Food, especially rice. (see káon).
(H) Sweets, sweetmeat, pastry, cakes, biscuits, bread, etc. (Almost any side-dish may be called "kalan-ónon", except rice, meat, fish and vegetables). (see káon).
A kind of very sticky, viscous rice; it is particularly used for making "íbus" and "alopí". (see arabón, pilít).
Unsymmetrical, awry, unequal, lop-sided, disproportioned, queer, odd, strange. Ang íya bísti kalandrákas. Her dress is unsymmetrical. She is dressed in an odd style.
(H) Ladle, scoop, shovel for dry or liquid things. (see kándus, luág, garaló).
(H) Abomination, frightfulness, repulsiveness, something shocking or terrifying, things awful to look upon, filthy stench. (see ngíl-ad, kangíl-ad).
That is to be pitied or regretted. (see kanógon).
(H) A song, lay, ballad, ditty, what is to be sung, a hymn, chant, canticle. (kánta; see ambahánon, ambáhan).
Perfection, quality of the highest worth, excellence, first class, supreme, things of the highest standard. (lántip; see kahimpitán).
To fill with water, mortify, get infected or purulent through the action of water, said of wounds, etc. Kinalantubíg ang ákon pilás. My wound mortified (through contact with water).
Associate, companion, cooperator, collaborator; at the side of, near-by, adjacent. (see tupád).
See kalápad.
(H) See kalápad.
Omission, neglect, negligence, failure to comply with orders, duties, etc. (see lápas).

Tendril of a vine, etc.; to encircle, wind around, cling to, entwine. Ang búyò nagakalápkap sa búgsok. The "búyò" is winding itself around the post. Iníng mga bató ginakalapkapán sang kadenadeamór. These stones are entwined with the vine called "cadena de amor". Pakalapkapá ang kalubáy sa palápála. Make the "calubay" cling to the trellis or lattice work. (see kápkap, kabúd).
Plaster, any kind of sticky or viscous material. (kápol).
(H) To be-castrated,-gelded, fit to be made-a "capon",-a eunuch (especially said of cocks). (see kapón).
(H) Place where animals are castrated. (see kapón).
(H) Anything used for grasping or holding. (kapút).
(H) Thickness, consistence, coherence, density, condensation, inspissation (of liquids). (see lapúyut).
Tiredness, fatigue, exhaustion, feebleness, weakness. (see lápyò, kabúdlay, kalúyà).
See kalás-ay. Also: Things that are insipid or cause nausea or aversion.
Shield, cover, protection, defense; escutcheon.
(H) See kalasálon.
Snare, trap, net; difficulty, trial. (see káti, katián).
(H) Meeting, assembly, club, club-house, society. (see típon).
A kind of cactus-tree with beautiful white flowers.
Evil, badness, wickedness, malice, malignity, maliciousness, malevolence, banefulness, balefulness, perniciousness, noxiousness; misery, wretchedness, misfortune. (see láut, kaláin).
(H) Ugliness, hideousness, unsightliness, unseemliness, nastiness, unbecomingness, impropriety, indecency. (see láw-ay).
(H) See kaláw-ay. Also: Things that are ugly, unbecoming, dishonest, indecent, filthy, improper.
A kind of plant. It is used as a remedy for painful or decaying teeth.
Body, the main or principal part of a dress, the contents of a letter (as distinct from the address), etc. (see lawás, ináng).
(B) Length, duration of time. (see kaláwig id.).
Length; distance. (see kaláwig, kalayoón).
(H) Pleasure, enjoyment, delight, satisfaction. (wíli; see kalawilihán, kawilihán).
(H) Anything used as a hook, as a stick or pole with a hook attached to it and the like. (kawít; see síngit, singít).
Exsiccation, withering, fading, drying up. Búlak nga walâ sing kalayaán. A flower that never withers. (see kalayâ).
Aridity, dryness; dry or arid soil. (see layóng).
(H) To be on fire, to flame or flare up (of fire; see hingaláyo, kaláyo).
See kaláyngan-aridity, etc.
(H) See kalayô.
(Sp. calvo) Bald, hairless. (see bungád, upáw).
(Sp. caldera) Kettle, cooking pot (of metal).
(Sp. caldero) A large kettle, bucket or tub (of metal).

(Sp. caldo) Broth, beef-tea, bouillon, sauce, gravy, a stew, a mixture of meat, potatoes, onions, sausages, etc. Also verb: Kaldohán mo akó sing kárne. Make me a dish of "káldo" from meat. Also: A large bowl or cup; saucepan. (see kaldóhan).
(Sp. calendario) Calendar, almanac. (see almanáki).
(Sp. calentura) A cold, fever. (see lágnat, hilánat).
(Sp. calesa) A kind of two-wheeled vehicle, covered-in buggy or gig.
(Sp. calesin) A small kalésa.
(B) The youngest (a younger) brother or sister; the last or youngest child of a family. Si Pédro amó ang íya anák nga kalibáynan. Peter is her youngest child. (see libáyon, kamanghóran, mánghud).

See kalibúg. Also: Mixture as between Visayans and Negritos, Visayans and Europeans, etc.; Mestizo, half-breed, hybrid. Ang mga bumulúthò nga tumándok nagpakigáway sa mga bumulúthò nga katsílà kag kalibugán. The native students fought against the Spanish and half-caste students.
Worldly, earthly, materialistic, sensuous, sensual. Ang mga táo nga kalibutánon. The worldly minded. Kalípay nga kalibutánon. Worldly or sensual pleasures.
See kalíg-on. Also: Security, bond, bail, anything that makes for stability or freedom from danger and apprehension.
(B) See kalígà. (see kalipátan).
Swiftness, speediness, celerity, rapidity, fleetness, nimbleness, agility, quickness of movement. (lígsi; see kalíksi).
(H) To stir, loosen up earth, rice in a kettle, etc. Kalikáda (kalikára) ang tiníg-ang. Loosen up the cooked rice. (see hakíd, súkad).
Anything used for cleaning out liquid waste matter from narrow tubes or holes, as from the ear, the nose, a wound, etc. (see kilikóg).
(H) Preoccupation, distraction, state or condition of being much upset or distracted by cares, etc.; things that make one's head swim, perplexity. (libúg; see kalibúg).
Fifty. (see limá).
The eyeball, the apple of the eye; the pupil of the eye. (see taótáo).
Plough-handle, plough-tail.
Folly, foolishness, stupidity; a stupid fellow.
Distraction, diversion, relaxation, entertainment, things apt to distract the mind and provide amusement. (see lingáw).
Apprehension of danger, hesitation, wavering.
See kalínyas-to wind on a bobbin, etc.
Bobbin; to wind on a bobbin. Ang bunáng ginakalínyas. Yarn is wound on a bobbin. Kalinyasá iníng isá ka labág nga kósta. Wind this hank of yarn on bobbins.
See kalípay. Also: Things that give pleasure, happiness or enjoyment.
(H) Anus. (see áno, kagalán, ipotán).
Lime-kiln; furnace. Ginbutáng siá níla sa kalirohán. They put him into the furnace (lime-kiln). (see kalíro).
Difficulties, distress, etc. See kalilísdan, lisúd, kalisúd.
See kalísding. Also: liability to tilt, possibility of tilting. Dílì ka mahádluk sináng bayóng, kay walâ gid inâ sing kalisdingán. Have no fear about that bamboo water-tube, for it cannot tilt over.
Backwardness, dulness, stupidity, condition of a person whose mental faculties are below normal. (see pungág, tampuháw, pákok, búngaw).

A kind of binding or fastening together with spaces between the pieces fastened together, as in the making of a "lág-i", of split-bamboo flooring, etc.; to tie, fasten or bind together after the manner of "kalítgit".
Clumsy, awkward, ungainly. (see baksiwâ, bikwálon).

To remove, get or take out, as bones from a mortuary niche, to dig out, look-, hunt-, up, data from a register or the like. Kalkalá ang linubúng. Disinter the buried corpse. Ginkálkal sang piskál ang sertipíko nga kinahánglan ko. The parish-clerk dug out from the register the certificate I needed. Kalkalí akó sang ákon sertipíko sang bautísmo. Look up and copy for me my baptismal certificate. Ikálkal akó ánay siníng panteón nga dáan. Please open and clean out this mortuary niche for me.

Cold rice warmed up and stirred in a pan either with or without lard; to warm up rice in the manner described. Kalókalóha ang kán-on. Warm the rice and stir it in the pan. Kalókalóhi akó sing kápog. Make me a dish of "kalókálo" from cold rice. Ikalókálo akó ánay siníng báhaw. Kindly prepare me a dish of kalókálo from this cold rice.

(H) To tuck or turn up (trousers and the like). Kalokúsa ang delárgo mo. Tuck up your trousers. Nagalakát silá nga kinalókus ang íla mga delárgo. They are walking with their trousers tucked up. Pangalókus ka, kay matabók kitá sa subâ. Tuck up (your trousers), for we are going to cross the river. (see baláking-to tuck up skirts, sotanas, and the like).
Any sticky, viscous juice.

(B) To compress, press together, squeeze between the hands. Angay gid nga kalomóon ni nánay ang úlo mo, kay nagsinutíl ikáw. It is quite right for mother to squeeze your head, for you have been naughty. Ginkalómò níya siá. He squeezed his head. (see kulámò).
Dry, exsiccated, empty, applied particularly to pods and husks; to be or become dry. (see kagúng).
One, one piece (of dry fruit enclosed in a pod or husk). Hatági akó sing isá ka kalóng nga kamúnsil. Give me a pod of camunsel-fruit.
Wart, wart-like excrescence.
To carry in one's arms. Kalongkongá ang bátà. Carry the baby in your arms. Ikalóngkong akó ánay siníng bátà. Please carry this baby in your arms. (see kúgus, kólkol).
To scratch (with the nails, claws, etc.). Kalosá siá. Scratch him. Ginsúmbag ko siá, kay kinalós níya akó. I struck him, because he had scratched me. (see karós id.).
See salók, kándus-to scoop up (out), draw water, etc.

To scratch softly (to ease an itchy feeling). Indì mo pagkalóton ang arikís mo, kay básì magadúgang. Don't scratch your rash, for it may become worse. Nagdágsang ang íya katúl, kay kinálot níya. His skin-disease "katúl" began to fester, for he scratched it. Ikálot akó ánay sang ákon likód, kay indi akó makadáb-ot. Please scratch my back for I cannot reach it.
(Sp. calzon) Drawers, pants, underwear, short trousers.

(H) Coconut-grove, coconut-plantation; self-praise, boastful language, bragging about one's accomplishment, etc. Nagasúgid siá sang íya nga kalubihán. He is boasting of his accomplishments, etc. (see lubí, kaniogán, agrót).

To scratch in the meaning of "kálot" but with this difference that "kalúbkub" indicates a swifter motion to and fro of the hands and fingers. Kalubkubá ang ímo katúl. Scratch your itch. Kalubkubí siá. Scratch him. Ikalúbkub akó sa ákon likód. Kindly scratch me on the back. (karúbkub, id.).
To cover or enwrap oneself, put a blanket, etc., round one's body. (see kalúmbut, pangulúmbut, panimúlon).

To swing, hang, dangle by the hands, with the feet off the ground. Ang mga amô nagakalumbítà sa sangá sang káhoy. The monkeys are hanging by their hands from the branch of the tree. Ang káhoy ginakalumbitá-an sang mga amô. The monkeys are dangling from the tree. (see kábit, kabítkábit).

(H) Cloak, coat, cover, wrapper; to cover or protect oneself against the cold, against blows and thrusts, etc., by wrapping a blanket, or the like, around one's body. Magkalúmbut ka sing hábul. Wrap a blanket around you. Ginkalúmbut níya ang hábul. He protected himself with a blanket. Ginkalumbután siá níla sing hábul. They wrapped a blanket around him. (see pangulúmbut which is more in use as a verb).
(H) Withering; destruction, ruin, perdition. (see lúmpag).
Drowning. See kalulúmsan id.
Mud, mire. (see lúnang).
See kalúya. Also: Things that are tiresome, exhausting or wearying.
See kalúya. Also: Things that cause weakness or that are debilitating.
Neighbour, friend, partner. (see kaluyó, kaíping, kasilíngan).
Pan, frying pan. (see kaláhà, karuágan, karwágan).
A little, small amount, trifle, bagatelle, insignificant, of little moment, of no importance. (see púdyot, diótay, tikî, ikî).
See káli.
(Sp. calle) Road, way, street, causeway, walk, row. (see dálan, kalsáda).
(Sp. callo) Callus, callosity, corn, wen. (see kíbul).
A large, thick bowl as used in Philippine households.
Pygmy, dwarf, fairy, pygmean ghost; dwarfish.
See kamág-an.
See kamág-o. Also: Things that have only lately been introduced, new fashions and styles and the like. (see kalamág-ohán id.).
The string with which a spinning top (kasíng) is spun.
Friendship, friend, intimate acquaintance, attachment, mutual esteem or assistance. (Often used rather humorously instead of the Sp. amistád).
(H) Suspense, doubt, hesitation. (see kalamalamahán).
Hut, shed, hovel, granary, storehouse.
The little finger. (see kumalíngking, tingayón, tingáy-tíngay).
A tree whose leaves are often boiled and used as a vegetable. (see balúnggay id.).
A kind of plant similar to "kásla", but with a reddish stem and dark leaves.
A kind of incense.
Openness, spaciousness; freedom to get a living and make progress. (see manháwà, kamanwaháan).
The Philippine breadfruit.
A kind of grass.
Prosperity, welfare, progress, success, well-being. (see manwáhà).
See kamanhawáan id. (see manwáhà-manháwà).
Thoughtfulness, regard, consideration, sympathy, kindness. (see pasunáid).
(Sp. canapé) Sofa, settee, lounge, couch.
(Sp. cámara) Hall, chamber, house (of a legislative body). Kámara álta. Upper House. Senate. Kámara báha (Sp. baja) Lower House. House of Commons.
(Sp. cámara) The cabin of a "lorcha".
(Sp. recámara) Mortar, shooting mortar, detonator.
(Sp. camarín) Barn, shed, outhouse, storehouse, go-down.
(Sp. camarote) State-room, berth; cabin (of a steamship, etc.).
Fight, scuffle, scrimmage; any limb, as an arm, leg, tentacle, etc., used in a fight. (see kámas).
(B) The last child in a family, the baby of a family; youngest brother or sister. (see kalibáynan, libáyon).
Greed, voraciousness, passion for. (see maóg).
Fertility (of soil); plenty, galore. (see maúya).

To encircle, wind around, entwine. Ikámbad mo sa ákon bútkon iníng tinábas. Wind this piece of cloth round my arm. Kambarí (-adí) ang bútkon ko sang bínda. Bind up my arm with the bandage. (see kámbat, kámbod, sabúd).
See kámbad. (see kambatí-kambarí).
To twist round the legs or feet as in wrestling, etc. Kambirí (-idí) siá. Entwine your legs around him. Ikámbid sa íya ang ímo tiíl. Twist your foot around him. (see sálbid, lákwid).

(Sp. cambio) Change, exchange, barter; to exchange, barter, swop, swap, change. Ikámbio ko iníng báka sa ímo karabáw. I will exchange this ox for your buffalo. Kambiohí iníng papél nga sínko písos sing sensílyo. Give me change for this five-peso bill. Nagkambiohánay silá sang íla mga baláy. They swopped houses. Ikámbio mo akó ánay siníng kwárta. Please give me change for this money. (see báylo).
See kámbad-to encircle, etc.
Stomach-or chest-protector, abdominal belt; cholera belt; armour, cuirass.
(Sp. cambray) Cambric; gauze, fine or transparent linen.

Unseemly, unsightly, slovenly, not well done (of sewing, etc.). Kambúsà (Nagakambúsà) ang ági siníng mákina, siníng talahían, etc. No good sewing is done with this machine,-in this tailoring shop, etc. Also: A kind of small dog with curly hair.
Change, exchange. See kámbio.
(Sp. camello) Camel.
We, excluding the person addressed or spoken to. See kamihánon, kamíkámi.
Dim. of kamí. (see kamihánon).

Tap, light stroke, gentle slap; to tap, slap, strike with the finger-tips. Kamiasá ang íya ilóng. Tap his nose. Indì mo siá pagkamiasán sa íya guyá. Don't tap him on the face. (see káblit, kúhit, kámlot, kámlò, tándog, kámlas, tápdas).
We among ourselves. (see kamí).
Capsized, overturned; to turn turtle, overturn. (see túmba, sulî, balískad).
(Sp. camino-road) Road-mender, street-cleaner.
See kamíngaw. Also: Things that make life lonely, sad, etc.
Loneliness, dejection, etc. See kamíngaw.
(Sp. camino) Road, way, street, causeway, walk, row. (see dálan, kalsáda).
A kind of fish. See tamínsot id.
(Sp. camiseta) Shirt-like blouse, spencer, short shirt, worn by men (without a coat).
(Sp. camisola) A shirt-like upper garment worn by women leaving the neck free; ruffled shirt, dicky. Also: night-shirt. (see báta).
(Sp. camisón) Long shirt, night-shirt, chiefly worn by women. (see báta).

To touch, nudge, bring one's hand in contact with. Ikámkam ang ímo kamót sa dalúnggan sang bátà. Touch the baby's ear with your hand. Kamkamá siá. Touch him. Kamkamí siá sa íya bútkon. Touch him on the arm. (see híkap, tándog, kámlot, etc.).
See kámias.

To nudge, touch momentarily. Kamloá siá. Nudge him. Kamloí siá sa kamót. Touch him on the hand. Indì mo pagkamloón ang líbro, kay básì mamansahán. Don't touch the book, for it may get soiled. (see kúhit, káblit, kámkam, etc).
(H) See kámlò. (kamlotá, kamlotí-kamloá, kamloí).

(B) To grasp, clutch, clench, grapple with, as in wrestling, etc. Nagakamogoláy silá. They are grappling with each other. Kamagóla siá. Grapple with him. Ginkamógol níya akó. He held me in a clench. Siá gid lang nga isá ang nagakamógol sang íya trabáho. He grapples with his work quite alone. (see kámog, gahús, gakám).
You among yourselves.

To encircle or span around with thumb and middle-finger. Indì siá makakamól sang ákon liwatán. He cannot span my wrist with his thumb and middle-finger. Tilawí kag kamolón ang ákon bútkon kon makasaráng ikáw. Try to encircle my arm with your thumb and middle-finger, if you can. Also: A handful, as much as one can grasp with thumb and middle-finger. Hatági akó sing isá ka kamól nga humáy. Give me a handful of rice. Metaphorically: Walâ gid sing nakadimól, kay gínúrut lang níya sang kamól. Nobody had any benefit of it, because he grasped (or took) everything for himself. (see gamól).
The thumb. (see kumalagkû).
(H) The hand. (see alíma).
(Sp. campanario) Belfry, bell-tower. (see lingganáyan).
(Sp. campanilla) A small bell, altar-bell.
A large, long kind of sword; hanger, cutlass.
(Sp. campo) Field, open ground, camp, campus. (see umá, patág, halampángan, halampangánan).

(B) To include all, embrace all, comprise all, take in all, leave out none or nothing; equipped, provided or dealt with, in an equal manner. Nagakámpod silá nga tanán sang páyong, sang kálò, etc. All of them have umbrella's, hats, etc. Ikámpod mo sa íla ang mga lápis sa látok. Distribute to them the pencils that are on the table. Kampodán mo silá sing bíntay nga mútyà. Give them all ear-rings made of pearls. Pakampodán mo silá nga tanán sing bág-o nga mga tulún-an. Procure new books for all of them. Kámpod (magkámpod) kamó nga tanán sang binángon kag maglakát. Take (all of you) your boloes and go. (see tápud, túptup).
(Sp. campeón) Champion; hero.
See kámara.
See kámlas, kámros id.
To tap, stroke, slap, etc. See kámlas.
Increase, multiplication, propagation, procreation, augmentation, production, growth, increment. (see búad, múad).

An equal, one of the same blood, condition or position; to be partners, help or stick together and never fight each other. "Nagakamúkhà silá" may mean "They are idiots or half-fools" or "They are partners and will not fight against each other". (see kaángay, kasúbung). (N.B. kamúkhà seems to be a Tagalog word).
Not quite normal, half-witted, fool, softy. (see kulángkuláng, buangít, tampuháw, etc.).
Apprehension, fear, misgiving, suspense, doubt. (see kalamalamahán, kamalamalahán, kahangáwà).
A kind of flower.
A kind of plant with very odoriferous leaves.

Beginning, start, commencement, first stage, introduction, initiation, preface. Sa kamunóan, kag (sa) katapúsan--. At the beginning, and at the end--. At any rate--. When everything is said--. Under all circumstances--. (see púnò).
A very common tree whose fruit is edible and whose wood supplies many a house with posts.
A kind of tall grass.
(B) To lead in work, direct work and take the chief hand in it. Sín-o ang nagakamúros sa ínyo nga pangabúdlay? Who is your leading workman? Or: Who is your boss?
Living from hand to mouth, etc. See abátabát.

(Sp. como está) How are (you)?; to greet, salute, shake hands, inquire after another's health, etc. Kamústa ka man? How do you do? How are you? Kamustahánay kitá ánay. Let us shake hands first. Nagkamústa siá sa ákon. He asked me how I was. He saluted me. He shook hands with me.

To strive, exert oneself, strain every nerve, do one's best, make great efforts; to fight, wage war, join battle, enter into conflict, engage in a fight. Nagakamútut (nagakinamútut) silá sa pagdaúg. They are making great efforts to win. (see pamurúg-ot, himúd-os, paningúhà, panikasúg).
A flowering plant.
(B) Article for the dative and accusative. (see sa, kay, sang, kang).
(B) When, at what time, (always with reference to the past). (see sán-o, pa, id.).
Food, especially cooked rice. (see káon).
(B) Him, her, it; to, at, from, by, etc. him, her, it. (see íya, sa, íya).
To test, try, examine, probe. (see tiláw).
(B) See kanabâ.
Test, trial, probe, examination, contest, competition. (see kaná).
(Sp. canal) Channel, ditch, trench, conduit. Also: Verb. Kanalí ang higád sang dálan. Make a ditch at the side of the road. (see kalóg, ililigán).
To do quickly, thoughtlessly, absentmindedly, unawares. Nakanalî lang akó sa paghámbal sinâ. I uttered that thoughtlessly. (see tabinás, dalî).
See kanámit id.
A kind of rice. (see arabón).
An exclamation of joy and pleasure: Oh, how nice! How lovely! What a beauty! This is fine! (see aráw, aráwaráw).
(B) To them, etc. Itúgro iní kanánday Pédro. Give this to Peter and his family, to Peter's household. (see kánday).
(Sp. canario) Canary (bird); yellow.
(Sp. canasto, canastro) Basket, hamper, crate, used for marketing fruits, vegetables, etc.

Slow, tedious, tardy, flagging; to be slow or tedious. Nagkánat ang ámon trábano sa umá sa karón nga túig, kay nagmasakít ang ámon mga háyup. Our farmwork has been slow this year, because our animals are sick. (see kúnat).
Dim. and Freq. of kánaw-to glisten, etc. Nagakanáwkanáw ang íya mga lúhà. His tears are ready to flow. His eyes are brimming with tears.
The North-West.
Great distance, farness, far away. (see nayóknáyok, nayópnáyop).
See kanáyok.
A cotton-plant with reddish or light brown flowers. (see búlak-a cotton-plant with white flowers).
(Sp. candado) Lock, padlock. (see pamakúd).
(B) To, for, towards, etc. them. (see sa, íla, kanánday, kanánda).
(Sp. candelero) Candlestick.
Candlestick. (see kandiléro id.).
Goat. Kánding nga laláki. Buck, goat. Kánding nga babáye. Nanny goat.
A kind of melon, or cucumber similar to the "atímon".
To form into lumps or balls. Ginakándol níya ang samblági. She is forming tamarind into balls. Kandolá ang tsokoláte. Make the cacao (cocoa) up into balls.

To shovel, scoop, spoon or ladle out dry and liquid things. Kandusá ang humáy, sópas, etc. Scoop out the rice, ladle out the soup, etc. Kandusí akó sing isá ka kándus nga sópas. Give me a ladleful of soup. Ikándus akó ánay sing duhá ka gántang nga humáy, kay ipíslong ko sa lusóng kag bayohón. Kindly scoop out two gantas of rice for me, because I am going to put it into the mortar and pound it. (see sarók, galó).
(Sp. canela) Cinnamon.
Driver of a wagon or bull-cart, waggoner, carter. (kángga).
(B) Mercy, compassion, sympathy, clemency. (see kaló-oy, kaáwà).
Terror, horror, frightfulness; terrible, horrible, frightful, awful, shocking. (see ngídlis).

(H) See kangíl-ad. Also: Things that are loathsome, sickening, noisome, abominable, detestable, nauseating, nasty, filthy, shocking to look upon or to hear of, the abomination or aversion produced by evil or by things of a very disagreeable smell. (see kalangil-arán).
See kangítngit. Also: Things that cause heartache, etc.
(Sp. cangrena) Gangrene, mortification. (see dágsang).
(Sp. canguro) Kangaroo.
Surprise, shock, etc. See kahanguyús, kuyús.
(B) Coconut-grove, coconut-plantation. (nióg; see kalubihán).
Nípà-swamp, nípà-plantation. (see nípà).
Small, dwarfish, undersized, stunted in growth. (see koridíg, daúldaúl, aríarí, agílagíl).
A kind of small-leaved "búyò" used for betel-nut chewing.
See kaníwang.

To be or sound hollow, empty, loose, shrivelled, shrunk, said of the contents of bottles, tins, nuts, shells, etc. Iníng ítlog, lubí, etc. nagakanô. This egg, coconut, etc. sounds hollow. Also: dull, foolish, doltish, stupid. (see búngkag, búngaw, pákok, etc.).
(H) See kanobô.
An exclamation expressive of regret for something lost or spoilt. A, kanógon inâ! Oh, that's a pity! What a pity!
To fray and break easily, said of threads and yarn in clothes, etc. Nagakanótnot gid lang ang báyò ko. My jacket is just fraying away. (see nátnat, nútnut, tâtâ, sarabusáb).
A kind of tree whose reddish seeds are used for medicinal purposes.
(Sp. cancel) Screen, (upright frame). (see biómbo).

(Sp. canción) A song, lay, ballad, ditty; to sing, to troll. Kansyoná ang "Adiós". Sing the song "Adiós!". Kansyoní akó sing bilyansíko. Sing me a Christmas carol. (see ambahánon, ambáhan, ámba, kalantáhon, kánta).
(Sp. cantero) Mason, stone-cutter, stone-dresser, bricklayer, builder in stone and brick.
Dog-vane, weather-cock; to call-, summon-, invite-, the wind (at sea, at winnowing rice, etc.).
(Sp. cantidad) Quantity, amount, sum. (see pilá, kapíd-an).
(Sp. cantil) A steep, precipitous rock. (see píl-as).
(Sp. canto) Edge, rim, brim, corner, margin, bevel, cant. (see binít, hamitán, bígki).
(Sp. canto) Song, hymn, chant. (see ambahánon, kalantáhon, kansyón).
Cantonese, pertaining to-, made in-, from-Canton in China, applied to a variety of textiles, silk-fabrics, poultry, etc., coming from China, especially from Canton.
Singer, cantor, chorister, choir-boy, especially one who sings in church. (see manugámba from ámba).

(Sp. cañon) Cannon, gun, field-piece; cannon-ball; the benches in a prominent part of the Church for the accommodation of the Authorities and principal Catholics are also called "kanyón" in some places. Also: Ravine, gorge, canyon.
(Sp. cañuto) A small pipe or tube, as the tube through which the wick passes in a lamp.
The end, last things, latter happenings, final outcome. (olíhi; see katapúsan).

To eat, take food, feed, fare, devour, despatch, mess. Kán-a iní. Eat this. Kán-i iní sing diótay. Eat a little of this. Pakán-a siá sing maáyo. Feed him well-or-Give him good food. Pakán-a siá sa pínggan. Let him eat off the plate. Pakán-i sa íya iníng mga páhò. Let him eat some of these mangoes. Indì ka magkáon siníng búnga, kay línghod pa. Don't eat this fruit, for it is not ripe yet. Anó ang kináon mo? What kind of food did you take? Ipakáon ko sa íya iníng kabúgaw kon makaúyon siá. I will let him eat this pomelo if he likes it. Walâ akó makatupús sang ginpakáon níya sa ákon. I could not stand the food he gave me. Iníng kalán-an ginakán-an sing duhá ka púlò ka táo sa tágsa ka ádlaw. Twenty men take their meals-, mess-, are fed-, in this dining room every day.

To stick or adhere to; to paste, smear, put on powder, etc. Nagapakáp-al silá sing pólbos sa íla nawóng. They are powdering their faces. Nagakáp-al ang pólbos sa íya nawóng. Her face is thickly covered with powder. (see ápol, kápol, pilít, pálhit).

To droop, hang down, be full of-, covered with-, laden with-, weighed down with-, fruit, be enshrouded as with a mantle. Nagakápà ang mga sangá siníng káhoy. The branches of this tree are weighed down, (being covered with fruit as with a mantle). Nagakápà gid lang sang búnga iníng páhò. This mango-tree is covered with and bending under the weight of its fruit. (see gápà).
See kapa-ít. Also: Things that are bitter or difficult to bear, crosses, trials, hardships, sufferings. (see kalisdánan, kalalát-an, kapipít-an, kalilísdan, kahil-ánan).
Dim. of kápa. Also: To slap the water with the hands as in swimming, flap the wings, throw about one's hands and the like. (see kapáykápay).
See kapág-on. Also: Things that are stable or give stability.
Rest, repose, quiet, peace. (see pahúay).
See kapahuáyan.
Slowness; dulness, stupidity, ignorance. (see pákok).
The closing or healing of a wound, etc. (see pinalían-the mark of a healed wound or ulcer, scar, cicatrix). (see pálì).
(Sp. capa magna) Prelate's mantle, called Capa Magna, a dignitary's long gown.
A wiping-, rubbing-, out, erasure, deletion, abolishment, destruction, disappearance. (see pánas).
Tranquillity, repose, peacefulness, stability. Walâ gid sing kapantagán ang ámon pangabúhì. Our life has no peace. We can never rest at ease. (see pántag).

Army, large crowds or numbers, hosts, great multitude assembled, throng; shoal (of fish); herds (of sheep, cattle, etc.); numerous army (of soldiers); any great assembly or collection of things or persons. (see panóng).
Great-grandfathers; forefathers, forebears, progenitors, ancestors. (see pápò).
The priesthood (in the concrete, priests, clerics). (see párì).
Failure, setback, drawback, fiasco, disappointment, want of success. (see páslaw).
Punctuality, fixedness, fixity, stability; certainty, sureness, exactness, preciseness. (see pát-ud).
Plain, campus, wide valley or open country. (see pátag, patág).
Forty. (see ápat).
Fatigue, tiredness, weariness. (see pául, kahiól, kaálay, kabúdlay).
Fin (of fish). (see sílik, sírik).
The wing of a bird. (see pákpak).
The papaw and its fruit. (see papáyas).
(Sp. café) Coffee.
(Sp. cafetéra) Coffee-pot.
Twin, twins, (said of men, animals, plants and things in general); grown together, joined side to side, double. (see dungán).
Number, quantity, amount, an undetermined aggregate of individuals, that may be either few or many. (see pilá-how many).
Compulsion; to be compelled or forced. Nagkapilitán siá sa-. He was compelled (forced) to--. (see pílit).
(Sp. capilla) Chapel, small church, village chapel. (see ermíta).
See kapíot, kapipít-an.
See kapísan.
(Sp. capital) Capital, chief or principal town; capital, principal, money invested or set apart for an enterprise. (see úlo-bánwa, pahunán, prinsipál).
(Sp. capitán) Captain; mayor, burgomaster, municipal president (in Spanish times).
To feel one's way, grope. (see híkam, etc.).
To twist or twine round, encircle, entwine, cling to (as ivy). (see kalápkap).
Poverty, penury, misery, impecuniousness, pauperism. (see póbre, kaimolón).
To crumble, fall to pieces, said of clods of earth, or the like. Nagakapólpog ang pugá. The clod of earth is crumbling. (see pólpog).

(Sp. capón) Capon, gelding, any castrated animal, but particularly applied to cocks, pigs and dogs; to emasculate, castrate. Ginkapón níla ang mga báboy nga palatambókon kag ilihawón. They castrated the pigs that are to be fattened and slaughtered. Kaponá ang idô. Castrate the dog. Nakabakál akó sing tátlo ka manók nga kinapón. I succeeded in buying three capons.

The marriage ceremony; the bride and bridegroom giving their mutual consent and pledging conjugal fidelity and immediately after joining hands, before the priest who solemnizes their marriage. Bagtingán mo silá sa kápot. Ring the bells when they clasp hands. Nagpakápot lang silá, ápang walâ pagbilóhi. They went through the marriage ceremony, but did not receive the nuptial blessing during the Holy Mass.
To stick or adhere to, paste, glue. (see dokót, pilít).
(Sp. capote) Overcoat, raincoat, mackintosh, macintosh. (see kúmbut, kúnup, kulámbot).

Select tobacco leaves used as wrappers for cigars. Dálhi akó sing maáyo nga dáhon sang tabákò, kay ikapóte ko sa ákon piokós. Bring me a choice tobacco leaf, for I am going to use it as a wrapper for my home-made cigar.
Tired, exhausted, weak, worn out, done up, fatigued, weary, knocked up, jaded, spent. Kapóy na siá. He is tired out. (see paúl, luyâ).
(Sp. cafre) A ghost or monstrous being alleged by the superstitious to take the form of a horrible giant.
(Sp. capricho) Caprice, whim, fancy, fad, craze, quirk, crotchet. (see luyáglúyag, lubá).
(Sp. cápsula) Capsule; metal cap on a bottle or the like.
Cold (cooked) rice. See kápog.
Nations, powers, states, governments. Ang mga kapungsurán sang kalibútan. The nations of the world. Ang katilíngban sang mga kapungsurán. The league (society) of Nations. (see púngsud).
Archipelago, island-group. (pulô). Ang Kapupúd-an nga Pilipínas. The Philippine Islands.
Islands, isles, archipelago. (see pulô, kapupúd-an).
Fulness, plenitude; abundance, plenty, affluence. (see punô).

Profit, utility, use, gain, avail, benefit, good, advantage, behoof, boot. Ang tanán náton nga mga paninguhâ manginwaláy kapuslánan, kon walâ kitâ pagabulígi sang Diós. All our efforts are in vain-or-of no avail, unless God assists us. (see pulús).
A kind of maize with black and white kernels mixed on the same cob.
To grip, grasp. See kapút. Kapyotí, kinapyotán-kápti, kináptan. (see úyat).
(B) See karón.
(B) Of that, etc. (see sinâ id.).
To come and go, visit frequently, go to and fro. (see karâ).

To burn lustily, crackle and spread (of fire). Ang kaláyo nagakarábkárab. The fire is burning lustily, is spreading, is increasing (with a crackling sound). Agólagól (kirótkírot) gid lang iníng kaláyo; butangí sing paámak, agúd magkarábkárab. This fire is burning low; put some kindling on it, that it may burn bright.
(B) Repairs, etc. See kilidanón, kaalayohón.
(B) Multitude, etc. See karakoán.
(B) Badly done, botched, bungled, clumsy, desultory, careless work. (see bástos, bául, patarásak).
Uneasy, nervous, excited; to be excited, nervous, etc. See darabáhan.
To cluck (of a hen). (see kurukutúk, katákkaták).
A kind of banana. (see lakatán).
(B) Multitude, great number, many, plenty, crowd. Ginpakahúy-an akó níya sa karakoán (karák-an). He put me to shame in public. (see rakô).
(Sp. caramelo) Caramel, unrefined sugar, usually of a brown colour and sold in square tablets that readily dissolve in water, etc.

To scuffle, scramble, fight, to compete eagerly for the possession of something. Nagakaramútot silá sa pagágaw sang mga bukáka-or-ginakaramutótan níla ang pagágaw sang mga bukáka. They are scrambling for the ripe camunsel-fruit. Indì kamó magkaramútot. Don't scuffle (scramble, fight). (see ális, árnis, áway, kámas).
Restless, fidgety, unsteady. (see matínong-steady).

To hang down, fall down loosely (of clothes that are too large, etc.). Nagakarápà lang ang íya bistído. Her dress falls down loosely (like a mantle-kápa), being too long and too wide, etc. (see kápa, kápà).
See kalapól.
(B) See kalalóton, kalalotón.
To tear-, scratch-, pull-, off quickly vines, creepers, an old thatched roof or the like; to tear the ground (of a galloping horse); to perform with despatch, do quickly. (see káskas).
One who is in a hurry, who "sits on needles", etc. (see kuratán).
(Sp. carretel) Spool, reel; rope-walk reel, rope-maker's twisting machine, rope-wheel, cable-wheel; to twist, make ropes. (see lúbid).
To punish severely, chastise. Ginkaratíl níya ang íya bátà, kay nagsinutíl. She punished her child severely, because it was very naughty. (see baká-báka, tarítári, kátad).
(Sp. carátula) Pasteboard, label, sign-board, advertisement.
Tortuous-, winding-, zigzag-, movement, twist, contortion, convolution; to crawl, creep, twist, contort, writhe, move along, as snakes, or the like. (see isíísi, tikô).
A kind of bird.
(B) Hook. (see kalawít).
(B) Buffalo. (karabáw id.).
Pertaining to a buffalo; like a buffalo. (see kinarabáw).
(Sp. carbón) Coal; papel de carbón-carbon paper.
(Sp. carrera) Career, profession; run, race; to race. Nagakaréra na ang mga kabáyo. The horses are racing, (are off), already. (see palangitánan, kabuhián, palúmbà).
(Sp. carreton) Wagon, cart, go-cart; wheel. Butangí sing karetón ang sibáy. Put wheels (or rollers) on the baby's chair.

(Sp. carga, cargar) Burden, load; to load, burden; to transfer, enter. Iníng kárga lakás kabúg-at sa ákon. This burden is too heavy for me. Ikárga iní sa ímo áwto. Put this in your auto. Ikárga akó ánay siní sa ímo karósa. Please put this on your cart. Pilá ang hinákay kon kargahán ko ang ímo káro sing napúlò ka pásong nga humáy? How much will the freight be, if I put ten bushels of rice on your cart? Ikárga sa libro ináng mga binunyagán. Transfer to the register the names of those baptized. Dílì mo siá pagkargahán sináng sáko, kay támà kabúg-at sa íya. Don't burden him with that sack, for it is much too heavy for him. Nalúnud ang sakayán, kay kinargahán sing támà. The boat sank, because it was overloaded. (see lúlan).
(Sp. carga, burro) A game at cards.
(Sp. cargador) Porter, carrier.
(Sp. cargamento) Luggage, baggage, goods, load, freight, merchandise, cargo.
(Sp. cargo) Office, duty, responsibility, charge; income, receipts. Kárgo y dáta. Receipts and expenditure.

(H) To come here, approach. Karí ka dirí-or-Kumarí ka. Come here. Walâ pa siá makakarí, or: makapakarí. He hasn't been able to come here yet. Pakariá siá sa madalî. Order him to come here at once. Indì siá saráng makakarí-or-makapakarí. He is unable to come here.
A kind of dish. (see karihán).
One who steps into-, walks into-, interferes with-, meddles in-, something carelessly or thoughtlessly; to be careless, etc. (see tarádag, túdag, tádag, lúdag).
Short and stout, stocky, stumpy, stubby, thickset. (see kiribúd, tipúngkò, búdul, pudól, karibudó).
(B) See karibúd.
Inn, restaurant, rest-house. Place where "karí" is made or sold. (see karí).
(B) See kalíkad-to stir or loosen up rice, earth, etc.
(Sp. caricatura) Caricature.
Intricacy, complication, complexity. (see rikót).
(Sp. carril) Rail-rut, rail, cart-way, furrow.
(B) Sweetness. See katám-is. (see rímis).

(B) Small, little, tiny things, tots. Pulús mga karintukáy ang mga nagaeskwéla sa ákon kláse sang toksóan. The children that come to my catechism-class are all very small. (see íntok, magágmay, magágming).

To gather, collect, bring together, join or associate with, mingle, mix, put together. Indì mo pagkariponón ang mga kabatáan nga magamáy kag dalágkù. Don't put the small children together with the big ones. Ginkaripón níla ang mga báka kag karabáw. They put the cows with the buffalloes. Kariponá silá nga tanán. Put them all together. (see símpon, dápon, upúd, abáy).
(Sp. carrillo) A small cart; toy-cart.
A small lobster. (see koritót, kiritót).
(Sp.) Carmel; Carmelite nuns; Carmelite monks.
(Sp. carmen) Carmelite order; scapular, scapulary. (see eskapuláryo).
(Sp. carnaval) Carnival.
(Sp. carne) Flesh; meat. (see kusúg, unúd).
(Sp. carnero) Sheep; mutton. Karnéro nga babáe. Ewe, a female sheep. Karnéro nga laláki. Ram, a male sheep.
(Sp. carro) Cart, wagon, wain.

To do something with great speed, to scamp work, perform in a hurry; hasty, careless (of work). Karó-karó nga pagtrabáho. Careless, hasty work. Indì kamó magkarókaró sa pagóbra sinâ. Don't scamp that work-or-Don't be hasty and careless in doing that. (see karógkárog, karótkot).
To rub or scratch with some force. Karobkobá ang batíis mo kon magkatúl. Rub the calf of your leg if it itches. (see kalúbkub id.).
To rub, rasp, scratch (one's hair, head, etc.); to scrape, scoop out, shell (coconuts, gourds, etc.). (see kódkod, kokód).
(B) To hurry, hustle, urge on. Karóga tána nga magpánaw ron. (padaliá siá sa paglakát). Urge him to go quickly.
A hustler. (see karóg-károg).
A wide-meshed basket, usually hung up on a wire or string and used for carrying various provisions.
See kalókos.
To rumple, tousle, tumble, jumble, put-, throw-, bring-, in disorder; rumpled, jumbled, complicated. Indì mo pagkarókosohón ang lánot. Do not tumble the hemp-fibers. (see gómon, gomón, korokosó).

(H) Now, at present, at the present-time,-day,-moment,-juncture,-occasion, presently, immediately, shortly, forthwith, anon, nowadays; before long, soon; adj.: present, current. Lakát kitá karón. Let us go now. Mapailóngílong akó karón. I am going to Iloilo soon. Sa súbung siní walâ akó sing tinión, ápang karón ugáling tatápon ko ang ímo kinahánglan. Just at present I have no time, but before long I will attend to your need. Sa karón nga mga tinúig--. At the present time, in the times we are living in--. Ang karón nga túig. The present or current year.

To scratch (one's head or the like). Ginkaróskos níya ang íya úlo sa kaákig, sa kabúlung, etc. He scratched his head in anger, in astonishment, etc. Dílì mo pagkaroskosón ang úlo mo. Don't scratch your head. (see kalós, karós).

To scratch or rub against a door (as cats and dogs do); to scamp work, perform carelessly, hurry, hustle, do something by tearing and pulling, by leaps and bounds. Ang idô nagakarótkot sang ganháan, kay malúyag siá magsulúd. The dog is scratching at the door, for he wants to come in.
(Sp. cárcel) Prison, jail; to imprison, confine. Karsilá siá. Put him in prison. (see bilánggò, pahúnong, bilanggóan, kalabóso, kalabús).
(Sp. cartera) Portfolio, writing case, pocket book, note book, letter case.
(Sp. cartero) Letter-carrier, postman, one who carries or distributes letters.
(Sp. cartilla) Primer, first book for children. (see katón).

(Sp. carton) Card-board, paste-board; paste-board cards as used in various games. Malúyag akó maghámpang sang lóte, ápang walâ akó sing kartón. I would like to play the game called "lote", but I have no cards for it.
(Sp. cartucho) Cartridge, cartouch.
A pan. (see kalwágan).
(Sp. carruaje) Equipage, coach, four-wheeler, usually drawn by horses.

To wager, bet, stake, lay, lay a wager, make a bet, put one's money on. Kasahí siá sing duhá ka mángmang. Bet him two pesos. Pilá ang ikasá mo sa íya? What is your wager with him?-or-How much did you bet him? (see kási).
Banana-plantation, collection of bananas called "sáb-a". (see kasagíngan).
See kasáblag. Also: a person or thing that is an obstacle, that prevents, etc.
See kasádia id.
See kasádia, kasadiáhan, kasadiahón id.

A kind of crab. As this crab is usually rather lean it has become a synonym for thinness, leanness, emaciation. Kaság nga táo. A man as lean as a casag-crab. Kakaság siníng táo! How scraggy this man is!
(H) Banana-plantation, collection of bananas. (ságing; see kasab-ahán).
See kasakít. Also: Torture, martyrdom, bodily pains or punishments, things that inflict great bodily pain.
See kasáklaw. Also: things that are irksome, unpleasant, irritating.
Sins, faults, errors, offences, transgressions, trespasses, wrong-doing, slips, mistakes, blunders. (see salâ, kasáypan).
Incongruity, discrepancy, inconsistency, awkwardness, inharmoniousness. (see salangiság).
Injury, damage, destruction, harm, havoc. (see samád, sámad).
(Sp. casamiento) Marriage, wedlock, wedding. Kasamiénto sibíl. Civil marriage. (Sp. casamiento civil). (see mínyo, pangasáwa, kasál).
Goal, end, result; benefit, advantage; consummation. (see sámput, alapután, kapuslánan, kahimoán).
Mixture, blending; common, joint. Dútà nga kasamwánan. A field that is the joint (common) property of several persons or of a whole community. (see sámò, salamuánan, salamuanán).
When, at what time (of the past). (see kán-o, sán-o, pa).
Explanation, exposition, clearing-up, a clear proof of, manifestation, publication, explication, the unfolding of the facts or throwing light on something obscure, etc. (sánag).
Daybreak, peep of day, dawn, first blush-, prime-, of morning, morning light, aurora, daylight in its initial stages, the time preceding sunrise. (see sánag, kasánag, kasanagán, kasanagón).
See kasánag.
A partner at play, especially in a game of cards. (see sángga, dápig, kadápig, kadámpig).
Width, etc. See kasángkad, kasangkarón.
Formerly, in times past, long ago. (see sádto, ánay, sang, úna).

Continuance, continuation, durability, permanence, persistence, lastingness, quality of lasting long, decision, determination. Ang katin-arán kag kasanyogán sang bánwa--. The prosperity and stability of the town, commonwealth, etc. Isilíng mo na ang kasanyogán. State now your final decision or determination. (sányog).
See kasaplídan.
One who is a party to an agreement or contract, a member of a meeting or board, a councillor. Kasápulbánwa. A municipal Councillor. (sápul).

Temperance, moderation, sobriety, soberness, restraint; enough, not too much and not too little. Ang kasarángan. Temperance. Ang birtúd nga kasarángan. The virtue of temperance. Kasarángan gid lang ang íya nga pagkabutáng. He has just sufficient property to live on. He is neither poor nor rich. (see saráng, kasarangán).
Impropriety, indecency, unbecoming conduct, unsuitability. (see sáw-a).
Fault, blame, mistake, blunder, slip, error that needs correction. (sawáy).

To recuperate, recover, get slowly better and stronger, improve in health and strength after an illness, be convalescent, convalesce. Nagakasáykásay na ang masakít nga bátà. The sick boy is now slowly recuperating, (improving, moving about again).
Errors, mistakes, fallacies, blunders, oversights, slips; faults, shortcomings, defects, imperfections, deficiencies. (sayóp; kasáypan id.; see kasal-ánan, kakulángan, katalángan).
See kasayopán.
(H) See kasayóran.
Explanation, exposition, elucidation, explication, clear statement, interpretation. (sáysay; see kasayóran).
(Sp. caserola) Pan, saucepan. (see kaláhà, kalwágan).
(H) Denseness, thickness, condition of ground cumbered with high grass, brush or undergrowth. (sí-ot; see kasiók).
See kasíbò. Also: Things that fit or suit exactly.
(Sp. casillas) Lavatory, privy, closet, latrine, jakes, W.C. (short for water-closet). (see lubô, komún).
Co-citizen, fellow-countryman, citizen, resident. (see bánwa).
Feeling, sentiment, regard, consideration; to have regard or consideration for. (see patugsíling, pasunáid, balatyágon).
To fool, cheat, play a trick to. Dílì mo pagkasináhan ang ímo isigkatáo. Don't cheat your neighbour. (see dáyà, límbong, lág-it).
See kasahót.
Spinning top. (see trómpo).
(Sp. casino) Clubhouse for social or political reunions. (see tilipunán).
(B) Eventide, nightfall, evening twilight. (sírum; see kasisídmon).
See kasírum.
See kasírum, kasisídmon.
Straitened circumstances, difficulties, troubles. (see síot, kapipít-an, kalalát-an, kalisdánan).

To tear or pull off as an old thatched roof, vines or the like. Kaskasá ang dáan nga atóp kag ilísan mo sing bág-o. Tear off the old roof and replace it with a new one. Ikáskas akó ánay sináng mga balágon. Please pull off those creepers. (see karáskas).
(Sp. casco) Hull, hold of a ship, hulk. (see dágpak).
A kind of plant much used for hedges and fences. (see kamándag).
Imperative passive of kasál.
Marrying, marriage, the celebration of marriages or nuptials; to marry, get married (of many). (see kasál, pangasáwa).
(Sp. caso) Case, cause (legal); result, event, occurrence, contingency. Walâ man sing káso. There was no result. Nothing happened.
Commandment, order, injunction, law, prescription, rules; testament. Ang dáan kag bág-o nga kasogoán. The Old and New Testament. Kasogoán-bánwa. Municipal ordinance. (see sógò, pagbulút-an).
A kind of tree with an edible fruit. The stone protrudes from the ripe fruit.
A Philippine folk-dance.
(B) Once. See makaisá.
(Sp. castañas). Chestnuts, chesnuts.
(Sp. castañetas) Castanets, castanettes.

(Sp. castigo) Punishment, chastisement, correction, castigation, penalty; visitation (of God); to punish, chastise, castigate, penalize. Kastígo inâ sang Diós. That is (was) a visitation of God. Kastigóha siá. Chastise him. Ikastígo mo sa íya iníng múlta nga duhá ka písos. Punish him with this fine of two pesos. (see sílot, gábà).
(Sp. castillo) Castle, fortress; imitation of a bombardment by letting off detonating fireworks tied to a bamboo-erection.
(A corruption of castañetas) Castanets. (See kastanyétas).
(Sp. castor) Castor, small vessel with a perforated top for sprinkling pepper, etc.; beaver (animal so called). Aseite de kastór. (Sp. aceite de castor) Castor oil.
(Sp. castoreño) A derby hat, felt hat, any hat made of cloth.
Quarrelling, bickering and biting; things fought or quarrelled about. (súay; see kasúay, kasuayón).
See kasubô. Also: Things to be grieved over; that causes affliction or sorrow; sorrows.
Rivers, river-system. (see subâ).
Entrails, bowels, guts, viscera. (sulúd).
See kasúdlan. Also: Contents; vessel, container, receptacle.
Anniversary, annual or yearly celebration. (sukát).
Cocks. (sulúg).
Current, torrent, flow, race, course, swift motion of water. (sulúg).
See kasúlgan.
(H) Loathing, aversion; abomination. (see kasúm-od, kasulómo).
See kasúm-od.
Nooks, corners, out-of-the-way places, secluded places. (see suók).
See kasutíl. Also: Naughty behaviour, wicked deeds, naughty practices, bad manners.
See kasutíl.
See katáas. Also: High dignity, things that are lofty or sublime.
See katáas.

To stretch on a frame or rod, as yarn previous to weaving; to stretch on the rack, figuratively or literally. Katáda (-ára) ang bunáng. Stretch the yarn. Ginkátad níla siá. They put him on the rack. They punished him severely.
A frame to stretch yarn on, etc. Walâ ko makátad ang bunáng, kay walâ akó sing katadán. I cannot get the yarn ready for weaving, because I have no stretching frame.
Straightness, directness, rightness. (see tádlung).
See katádlung. Also: Straight-forwardness, honesty, rectitude, uprightness; honest and upright dealing.
Retiredness, shyness, bashfulness, coyness; to be shy, etc. May katág-an siá-or-nagakatág-an siá sa paghámbal. She is too bashful to speak. (see tágò).
Hearts; kind, sympathetic people, tender-hearted folks. (see tagiposóon).
See katahúm.
Reverence, deference, respect, veneration, esteem; distinction, glory, honour, dignity. (see táhud).
To cackle. Ang mungâ nagakatákkaták. The hen cackles. (see kákak, kurukutúk).
See katáksan.
To hang down freely, dangle loosely, (particularly applied to the male organ of generation of a horse or other animal).
(H) One of the same class or condition. Si Fuláno katalarúngan ko sa pageskwéla. N.N. is my classmate at school. (see dungán).
See katálaw.
(Sp. catalina) A wheel with teeth, cog-wheel, sprocket-wheel, spur-wheel.
The last part or stage of a thing, end, termination, condition of approaching ripeness, completion or termination. (see tápus, talipuspusón).
See katalúm.
Jungle, deep forest, bush, wild country, uninhabited territory. (see tálon, katalunánan, )
See katalúnan.
See katám-is. Also: Objects that are sweet, etc.
See katám-is.
Field, cultivated land, farm, especially rice-land. (see tánum, tanúm, palangúmhan).
Wonder, miracle, prodigy, marvel; wonderful, marvellous, miraculous, extraordinary. (see tanhágà, katingaláhan,
To live independently, have a household of one's own, live together with others. Pilá kamó nga nagakataó sa ínyo baláy? How many are you living together in your house? (see táo).
Men, mankind, humanity, the human race, man (taken collectively). (see táo).
Fragility, frailty, brittleness, weakness, flimsiness, quality of-being easily broken or torn,-having neither strength nor solidity. (see tapúk).

Justice, equity, justification, righteousness; argument, reason, contention, reasoning, argumentation. Ginpaháyag níya ang íya nga katarúngan. He gave his reason. He explained his argument. (see tárung).
To fray, etc. See kasâsâ id.
Mermaid, naiad, siren, water-nymph.
See katáwhay. Also: Things that make for a tranquil life, for peacefulness, etc.
Farness, distance, remoteness. (see táyog, kanáyop, kanáyok).
(Sp. cate) A measure for sugar, etc., equal to about two thirds of a kilo. (gm. 632.60). One hundred "káte" make a "píko" or "píkul" (Sp. pico).
(Sp. catedral) Cathedral.
(Sp. catequista) Catechist.
(Sp. catecismo) Catechism, christian doctrine. (see toksóan).
Glass, crystal. (kátyà id).
Possibility, feasibility, facility, occasion, opportunity (of obtaining or procuring a thing). (see katigayónan).
Procurement, preparation, effectiveness; capacity or ability to bring something about or to get results. (see tigáyon).
Place overgrown with tígbaw-reeds. (see tígbaw).
(H) The old, aged, superannuated, old folks, old people, parents advanced in age, forefathers, ancestors, ancients, by-gone generations. (see tigúlang).
Old age, oldness, senility, advanced age, superannuation. (see tigúlang, kagulangón).
Lure, bait, etc. See katián.
(H) Union, gathering, collection, assembly, meeting, society, resume, selection, anthology. (see tingúb).
Freedom, liberty, independence; the common people, ordinary folks. (see timáwà).
Reaching to below the knees, but above the ankles, short (of dress); a few inches above the ground, not reaching to the floor (of curtains, or the like).

To squat down in such a way that one does not quite sit on the ground. Indì ka magkatínkátin sa simbáhan. Indì mo pagkatínkatínan ang simbáhan. Don't squat down in church. Indì ka magkatínkátin, kóndì magtíndog ka kon may bisíta. Don't squat down, but stand up, when visitors are present.
Union, reunion, etc. See katilíngban. (see tingub).
See katíngban, katilíngban.

Union, society, association, assembly, meeting, gathering, club. Ang Katipúnan. The revolutionary society founded by Filipino Patriots during the latter part of the nineteenth century and directed against the Spanish colonial Government. (see katípon, katilíngban, tilipunán, tinipóntípon, talapuán, talapuánan).
A kind of coarse native cloth made in various colours that soon fade.
Small, insignificant, worthless. (see katitíya).
Dangers, perils, jeopardy, hazard. (see tiwálwag).

To find out about other people's affairs, to fish-, worm-, ferret-, out secrets and reveal them, to disclose, lay open, divulge. Katkatá ang sekréto ni Fuláno. Try to fish out N.N.'s secret. Kinátkat níya siá. He wormed out his secret. Sagád gid siá magkátkat sang mga tinágò sang ibán. He is an adept at worming out the secrets of others (and revealing or telling them to others).
Thirty. (tátlo).
