Hospitable, keeping open house, liberal in entertaining guests, treating visitors well. (amóma).
Helping, helpful, giving support; partner, party-man. (see ámpin, umalapín).
Watchful, keeping-watch,-vigil,-late hours; one-who stays (sits) up late,-who keeps watch and ward over. (see amoláw).
See maántod.
Shy, bashful, timid, retired, afraid, apprehensive. (see antorô, mahulúy-on, mahuyáon, mahádluk).
(B) Smelling like burning feathers, bones or paper. (see ántung).
Patient, enduring, tolerant, inured, suffering, bearing, tolerating, sustaining. (see ántus).
Helpful, assisting, succouring, aiding, protective, defensive, defending, protecting. (ápin, umalapín, mainapínon).
Insufficient, desultory, of little or no use, too little, of no avail, not adequate. (see kabús, kulábus, kúlang, higúshigús).
(B) Resentful, etc. See maaligotgotón.
Satisfactory, neither rich nor poor, rather well-to-do, well off. (see dawâdawâ, dirâdirâ, hingánhingán).

(B) Smoky, smoking, full of smoke, giving off much smoke, fumy, smouldering. Maáso nga digamohán. A smoky kitchen, a kitchen full of smoke. Maáso nga káhoy. Wood that gives off much smoke when burned. (asó).
Compassionate, sympathetic, commiserating, condoling, pitiful, clement, taking pity on, merciful. (áwà)

(B) Plump, large and stout, large in circumference, said of persons and things in general. Mabahúl nga táo, kalát, káhoy, baláy, etc. A stout man, a thick rope, a big tree or large piece of wood, a large house, etc. (bahúl) Also: rough, coarse, ill-mannered. (see dakû, madámol, bástos, manól, )
(H) Coarse, rough, uneducated.
Sweating, etc. See mabinalháson.
Grateful, appreciative, thankful; giving "tit for tat". (see bálus).
Sickly, infirm, weak (of health); liable to catch a disease. (see bátì, balatían).
Grateful; making a fitting return. (see bálus, mabinalúson, mabáslon).
Opining, guessing, surmising, calculating. (see bántà).
See mabinalúson-grateful, etc.

To be pregnant, to bear, be (big) with child, be in the family way, be in a delicate or interesting condition. Nagamábdus siá. She is with child or pregnant. She is in a delicate or interesting condition. Ginpamábdus siá ni Fuláno. She was with child by N.N. (see dála, búsung, sámbol, búntis).
Combative, pugnacious, quarrelsome. (see báis).
Concerned about, careful, watchful, taking a great interest in, bestowing great attention on, solicitous for. (see baláka).
Sweating, sweaty, perspiring, oily, one who perspires much and often. (bálhas).
One who reads or studies much, studious, well-read, bookworm, book-learned, given to reading. (bása).
Sentimental, sensible, sensitive, feeling, easily affected, delicate, susceptible of a sensation or feeling. (see bátyag, balatyágon).
Affable, friendly, conversing amicably. (búgno).
Moon-blind, purblind, dim-sighted, not quite clear, indistinct, misty, blurred, bleared. Mabinulánon ang íya panúluk. His sight is dim, he does not see clearly. (see búlan, bulánon).
(H) Curious, inquisitive. (see busísì).
(H) Inclining towards; inclined, accustomed, inured, habituated, disposed. (see buyó).
Shy, bashful, timid, reticent, quiet. (see budóng).
Fruitful, plentiful, prolific, teeming, crowded, thick, studded, galore. (see bugánà).
Admiring, astonished, with wonder or amazement, surprised, in surprise. (see búlung).
Fruitful, productive, prolific, giving (good) results. (see búnga).
Fragile, breakable, brittle. (see búung).
From malá-to dry, etc. (see málhan, mál-an).
Dense, thick, full of foliage, leafy, bushy. (dábung).
See madagáang.
Continual, constant, persevering. (see dáyon, madinayónon).
See madámpig.
Slippery, greasy, very smooth, not providing a firm foothold. (dánlog).
See madampígon, mabulígon, mabinulígon.
(H) Self-willed, overbearing, insolent, proud, arrogant, imperious, domineering, dictatorial. (see daúg).
(B) Good, well, nice, beautiful. (see maayád, maáyo).
Running, racing, hurrying, coursing, careering, flying, hastening, rushing along. (see dalágan).
Affectionate, caressing, petting, fondling, fond, kind, tender. (see dálò, mapinalangáon).
Dreamer, visionary; dreaming, dreamy, vague. (see dámgo).
Pernicious, nefarious, injurious, obnoxious, bad. (see dáut).
Cheating, tricksy, etc. See madáyà id.
See madalayónon.
See madinuhúl-dúlon.
Passing-, transferring-, sending-, handing-, a thing on, or to, someone else; a tell-tale, chatterbox. (see dóhol).
Thoughtful, recollecting, regardful, remembering, mindful. (see dúmdum).
Hating, spiteful, malignant, malevolent, vindictive, vengeful, rancorous, full of ill will, bearing a grudge. (see dumút).
Inclined, leaning towards, prone, warped, biased, prejudiced, predisposed, disposed, bent upon. (see dúyug).

A gale, squall, stiff breeze, blast, a cap of wind; violent, strong, blustering (of wind). Nagmádlus ang hangin. The wind blew strongly. Ginmadlusán kamí sang hángin sa sakayán. We encountered violent winds while we were on the boat.

To become fully awake, wide-awake, to get one's thoughts clear, to wake up. Walâ pa siá makamádmad kag namáhaw na. He is not yet quite awake and has taken breakfast already. Nakamádmad na ikáw-or-namadmarán na ikáw? Are you now wide-awake, are you quite clear in your head? (see marásmas).

Liable to be adhered to, susceptible of, amenable to, not unlikely to catch, apt to incur. Iníng táo madolókton sang ínit. This man is very liable to change colour (to become very red in the face, or the like) through exposure to the heat of the sun. (see dokót).
(Sp. madre) Mother; sister of a religious order or community; nun. (see ilóy, nánay).
(Sp. madrina) Godmother. (see manínay).
Dim. of madulúm. Dim, dusky, rather dark.
See madúmut-full of hate, etc.
Full of hate, spiteful, vindictive, rancorous, malignant, malicious. (see dumút).
Full of hate, etc. See madúmut.
Rotting, decaying, decayed, carrion, decomposing, putrifying, putrid, rotten. (see dúnut, dunút).
(Sp.) Teacher (female). (see maéstro).
(Sp.) Teacher; master, boss. (see manunúon, magtutúon, manunúdlò).

A prefix used chiefly in the following ways: 1) to denote the active infinitive, e.g. Hándà na kamó maglakát? Are you now ready to set out? Malúyag akó magtán-aw sinâ. I want to see that. Magtuón ka magsulát sing maáyo. Learn to write well.  2) to form the active imperative, e.g. Maghalín ka dirâ. Be off. Go away from there. Magtúman ka siní. Do this. Fulfil this faithfully. Magkáon na kamó. Now, eat your meal. Go to dinner. Indì ka magbúhat sinâ. Don't do that. Dílì ka magsúgid sinâ sa íya. Don't tell him that.  3) To form the active negative with "índì", expressing a disinclination, objection or lack of intention, e.g. Indì akó magbayó. I am not going to pound rice. I will not pound rice. Nanáy, si Hosé índì magtúman sang ímo nga ginsógò. Mother, José is not doing-or-will not do what you told him. Dì (dílì) siá magtámbong, konó, sa ámon bádù. They say that he is not taking part in our entertainment.  4) To form the past active negative with "walâ". Walâ siá magabút. He did not come. Walâ siá magkádto dídto. He has not gone there. Walâ pa siá magpanyága. He has not had his dinner yet.  5) to form nouns (frequently by reduplicating the first syllable of the root, e. g. magtutúon-teacher (tuón); magbubúlung-doctor, physician (bulúng); magsusúlat-writer (sulát); mag-amáy-father; mag-anák-child, son, daughter; mag-ilóy-mother; magluyó-partner; etc. etc.

To lighten, be or become light of weight, to alleviate, relieve, ease, mitigate, assuage, levitate. Buhíni ang ímo lúlan túbtub nga magmág-an. Lessen your burden till it becomes light. Nagmág-an na ang ákon kalisúd-or-namag-anán na akó sang ákon kalisúd. My trouble has now become easy to bear. Mag-aná sing diótay ang ímo dalá, kay támà kabúg-at. Lighten your load a little, for it is too heavy.
Married, the married persons. Ang mga mag-asawá. Those that are married. Married people. (see asawá, magtiáyon).
See pamág-o-to be new to a place, etc. (see bág-o, hínlaw).
Decaying, decayed, rotten, decomposed, dilapidated, ruinous, falling to pieces. (gabók).
Small, little, tiny, wee, diminutive, slender, thin, fine. (see magamáy, gágmay).
Dim. of magágmay. Rather small, etc.
The best of a bad lot, the least objectionable among a number of things or persons not coming up to the standard. (see gahîgahî).
Averse to noise or boisterousness, unsociable, retired, one who keeps aloof from the bustle, noise and strife of social life. (see gamó).
A rice-harvester, reaper. (áni). (see mangalaní).
A kind of tree, whose leaves somewhat resemble those of the tamarind.

A verbal form of anó. With "bisán (kon)"-However--. Whatsoever--. Bisán (kon) maganó kadakû ang (sang) íya kinaádman--. However great his learning may be--. Whatever (whatsoever) the extent of his learning--.
Tax-gatherer, toll-taker, collector of customs. (buhís).
Violent, ferocious, brutal, fierce, cruel; wild, not tamed, uneducated. (see maísug, mapíntas, mabangís, mailá, simarón).

This term seems to be employed only after a negative particle (índì, dílì) and then conveys the meaning of: very loud, uproarious, boisterous, so as to interfere with any ordinary conversation, etc. Dílì maghilibátì nga ulán, dagúob, etc. A very heavy downpour of rain, a very loud thunderclap, etc. Waláy lábut sang índì maghilibátì nga sinínggit sang mga táo--. Notwithstanding the deafening shouts of the men--. (see batî).
Cloudy, full of clouds; beclouded, confused, fuddled. (see gálum).
Boa constrictor.
The feminine of magkulumpariháy. (see kompári, komári).
A poisonous viper; a kind of basilisk (alleged to have a horn or comb and to crow like a cock).
Those related to each other by a spiritual alliance, as by means of Baptism or Confirmation. (see kompári).
Teacher, instructor, master, professor, preceptor, tutor, pedagogue. (tuón; see manunúon).
Hungry, famished, voracious, a great eater or feeder, one who wants to eat very frequently. (see gutúm).
See mahádluk, mahaladlúkon.

Dear, high-priced, expensive, costly, precious, esteemed, valuable, estimable; to make or become dear, cost much; to appreciate, esteem highly. Nagmahál na ang humáy. Rice has become dear. Mahalá ang ímo ginabalígyà. Sell your wares dear or at a high price. Indì mo siá pagpamahalán siníng mga sapátos nga ímo ginabalígyà. Don't sell him your boots at a high price. Kon dílì mahál báklon ko iní. If it is not dear I'll buy this. Ang Mahál nga Diós. The good God. Ang Mahál nga Bírhen. The Blessed Virgin. Minamahál ko nga ábyan. My dear friend.
(H) Afraid, timid, fearful. (see hádluk, mahádluk, mahadlúkon).
(H) Out of breath, panting-, gasping-, for breath, short of breath, breathless, wheezing, one who soon becomes exhausted for lack of breath. (see hápò, mahapoón).
(H) Metaphorical, figurative, in the form of a comparison or illustration. (see halimbáwà).
Wet, damp, moist, dank, dewy. (hám-ug).
Peaceful, tranquil, happy, quiet, felicitous, blessed; abundant, plentiful, fruitful, plenteous, teeming, copious. (see hamungáyà).

Out of breath, short of breath, breathing hard, panting-, gasping-, labouring-, gulping-, for breath, breathless, winded, blown, wheezing; liable to suffer from shortness of breath. (see hápò, mahalapoón).

Nice, beautiful, perfect, flawless, unblemished, faultless, uninjured, without flaw or defect; to be or become nice, etc. Tagái akó sing isá ka pánid nga mahî (mamahî) nga tabákò, kay himóon ko nga kapóti. Give me a flawless tobacco-leaf, for I am going to use it as a wrapper. Nagmahî na ang guyá sang bátà. The child's face has developed beautifully,-has become nice, or the like. (see mamahî, ayóáyo, maayóáyo, hímpit, lántip, gayón, ányag).
Dim. and Freq. of mahí-to be or become nice, etc.
Friendly, affable, kind, amiable. (see ábyan).
Knowing, wise, sapient, learned, experienced, clever, dexterous, skillful. (see hibaló, aláman, manginalámon, maábtik).
Home-sick, yearning to see, longing after, wishing to meet or see absent friends and relatives, nostalgic. (see hídlaw).
Opportune, convenient, advisable, proper. (see kahigayónan, kahigayonán).
Loving, tender, kind, warm, affectionate, tender-hearted, full of kindness and tenderness. (see gúgma, higúgma).
Less or smaller than required, not as large as, not enough, not quite sufficient, below the size or standard of a thing serving as a comparison. (see higúshigús, kúlang, kabús, kulábus).
See mahíkaw.
Meddling, interfering, meddlesome, officious, intrusive, apt to intervene or take part in; a busybody. (see lábut, hilabút).
Fornicating, lecherous, lustful, lewd, unchaste. (see hiláwas, maúlag, mahigál, hiwalán).
Yearning after, longing for, etc. See mahidláwon.
Retaliating, revengeful, longing for-, taking-, revenge, resentful, vengeful, vindictive. (see bálus, himálus, himalús).
Glorious, blessed, blissful, happy, enjoying the happiness of heaven; splendid, grand, brilliant, fine. (see himáyà).
Energetic, diligent, active, making great efforts, vigorous, striving hard. (see himúd-os, mapísan, maúkud, matinguháon).
See mahimulús. Also: taking advantage of, profiting by, making good use of an opportunity.
See mahimulúslon id.
See mahimúnung id. (himúyung-himúnung).
Hurtful, something that hurts, inflicting pain, painful; spiteful, revengeful, vindictive. (hinakít, sákit, sakít).
Intelligent, apt, smart, sharp or quick of understanding, grasping readily an idea or insinuation. (hangúp).
Ready, prompt, getting things ready, providing, provident, thoughtful, preparatory, prepared. (see hándà).
Ambitious, desirous, covetous, anxious. (see hándum).
See mahinalángpon id. (hangúp).
See mahinalángpon-intelligent, etc.
(H) Liberal, generous, free, munificent, bountiful, open-handed, giving freely, not stingy. (see hátag, maálwan).
Pursuing, prosecuting, persecuting, revengeful, vindictive, aggressive, hostile; hankering after, desirous, ambitious. (see hingabút).
Desirous of, wishing for, wishful, wistful, craving, hankering after, yearning for, longing for, covetous, ambitious. (see hingamó).
(H) Spending much, wasteful, prodigal, lavish, extravagant, spendthrift, making great out-lays in money, etc. (hinguyáng; see magásto, palagásto).
Home-sick, nostalgic, feeling out of sorts in a new place or in new surroundings, not growing well in new soil (said especially of plants transferred to another site). (see hínlaw, mahidláwon).
Compassionate, tender, mild, merciful, commiserating, condoling, kind, clement. (see hinóklog, malolóy-on, maawáon).
Repentant, penitent, contrite, regretting, remorseful, sorry for past wrongs or mistakes. (see hinúlsul).
Thoughtful, pensive, mindful, heedful, careful, wary. (see hunâhúnà).
A little naughty, rather mischievous; a little rascal. (see huróng).
Well ordered, well regulated, inclined to order, averse to disorder, orderly, regular. (see húsay).
See mahípus.
Miserly, stingy, closefisted, niggardly, mean, parsimonious. (see híras, maímot, maínot).
Home-sick, nostalgic. See mahinláwon.
See mahísà.
Helping, helpful, cooperating, assisting one another, in agreement, harmonious, united, working in unison for the common good. (see hiúgyon, mabinulígon, matinatabángon).
Fragrant, etc. See mahamút.
Weak, feeble, frail. (see húbol, malúya, malumíng, mapígaw).
Stirring, moving, restless, vicious. (húlag).
Cheerful, jolly, hilarious, frolicking, jubilant, merry, mirthful. (see húgyaw).
See mahún-og. (hún-ob-hún-og).
(H) See mahulúy-on-shy, shame-faced, etc.

To guess, conjecture, surmise, suppose, think, imagine, judge, opine. Sa ákon pagmái-om--. According to my opinion or guess--. Anó, ang namai-omán mo sa íya nahanungúd sang pagkasúnug sang íya baláy? What is your conjecture about him as to the burning down of his house? Mai-omá sing maáyo, básì malagpatán mo ang matúod. Make a good guess, perhaps you may hit on the truth. (see bánà, bántà, hunâhúnà, pakót, lágpat).
(H) Sack, bag especially one made of buri-leaves and used to pack sugar. (see bayóong).
Covetous, ambitious, etc. See maíbug, maibugón.
See maíbug.
See maíd-id.
(H) Desirous, covetous, wanting very much, avid, fond of, having a liking for. (ílà).
Sensual, sensuous, lustful. (see íbug, maíbgon, maíbug).
(H) See mailáon id.
Following, imitating, imitative, copying, aping, mimicking. (see ílog, ilógilóg).
Dim. of mailóm.
Patient, long-suffering, forbearing, forbearant, enduring, tolerant, tolerating, bearing with, putting up with, overlooking, undergoing pains, trials, etc., without complaint. (see ílub).
Friendly, amicable, companionable, amiable, sociable. (ábyan).
Affable, sociable, conversing amicably, friendly. (see áblaw).
An early riser, rising early, up early, up betimes, starting work in the early morning. (see agáp).
Hospitable, charitable, looking after the needy, kind to visitors, receiving them with an open heart and hand. (see ákup, inakúp).
Undecided, wavering, hesitating, etc. See maalág-ag).
Helpful, sympathetic, compassionate, ready to assist those in need of shelter or food. (see ayóp).
Feigned, pretended, sham, fake, put on, make-believe, hypochondriac, pretending, applied to illness as well as to the one that feigns or imagines himself to be sick. (see áloy, aloyán).
Devout, praying much, pious, man of prayer, given to prayer, prayerful, devout, contemplative. (see ámpò).
Contributing, generous, liberal, open-handed. (see ámot).
Warlike, martial, anxious or ready for a fight, pugnacious. See maawayón.
(H) Mending, repairing, patching up. (áyo).
Self-respecting, formal, modest, decent, proper, not frivolous. (see úgdang, maúgdang).
United, in unison, closely attached to each other, cooperating, collaborating, pulling well together. (see úgyon).
Scoffing, jeering, jibing, mocking, making, game of, jesting, deriding, ridiculing. (see uligâ).
Angry, cross, furious, wild, rabid, irate, apt to become angry, etc. at the slightest provocation. (see ugút).
Scoffing, mocking, insulting. (see úmpit, mainuligáon).
Joking jesting, mocking, making game of, making a butt of, ridiculing. (see úslit, uslitán).
Circumspect, careful, diligent, zealous, assiduous. (see úti, mautihón).
(Sp. maiz) Maize, Indian corn, corn.
Selfish, egotistic. (see íya-his, etc.).
(H) See makabibígne.
(H) Causing deafness, deafening, ear-splitting. (see bungúl).
Having power or authority, powerful, mighty, potent, ruling, holding sway, influential, puissant, strong, great. (see gahúm, gamhánan, makaákò).
See makagalánya.
(H) See makahahádluk.
(H) Uncanny, weird, queer, unearthly, causing an uncanny or weird feeling. (see hágnop).
(H) Delightful, delicious, pleasing, pleasant, funny, ridiculous, laughable, exciting laughter, comic, comical, amusing, exhilarating. (see hám-ut).
(H) Shocking, awful, terrible, dreadful, tremendous. (see kuyús, hanguyús, makahahádluk).
(H) Tickling, itching, titillating, irritating; exciting, disturbing. (see hilás).
Poisonous, venomous, baneful, virulent. (see hilô).
Loathsome, abominable, shameful, filthy, dirty, making one blush. (see hígkò).
See makahihílò.
Shameful, disgusting, disgraceful, exciting shame, putting to shame. (see huyâ).
(H) Intoxicating, inebriating, causing drunkenness. (see hubúg).
(H) Grievous, painful, distressful, distressing, afflicting, afflictive, causing pain and grief, sorrowful. (see kághà, makahanúsbò).
(H) Awful, fearful, tremendous, terrific, terrible, horrible, horrid, inspiring fear or terror, frightful, shocking. (see kúgmat, makalilísang).
(H) Intimidating, abashing, disconcerting, causing nervousness or shyness. (see kúlbà).

(H) Gladdening, gladsome, cheering, cheerful, joyous, joyful, inspiriting, sprightly, blissful, happy, gay, causing joy and gladness. Ipalánog nínyo sa madalî ang makakulúnyag nga balítà. Publish at once the joyous news. (see kúnyag, makalilípay).
Distracting, diverting, amusing, providing relaxation or diversion, entertaining. (see lingáw).
Exciting compassion or sympathy, miserable, wretched, poor, pitiful, piteous. (ló-oy).
Emitting a stench, stinking, evil-smelling, fetid, nauseating, abominable, horrible, exciting loathing or aversion. (see lóod).
(H) Ruinous, destructive, reducing to misery, leading to poverty. (see músmus).
A kind of rice ripening rather late and usually harvested during the month of December. (see arabón).
Six times. (ánum).
See makangingídlis-shocking, etc.
Loathsome, etc. See makangingíl-ad.
Four times. (ápat).
(H) Tiresome, exhausting, tiring, fatiguing, toilsome, wearisome, causing fatigue. (pá-ul, pául).
(H) Dreary, weary, sorrowful, causing grief or sorrow. (see púng-aw).
(B) Diligent, handy, obsequious, prompt and willing (of servants or the like). (see mapísan, matándus, sagád, maábtik, batíd).
(H) Horrible, terrible, etc. See makabibígne.
(H) Touching, affecting; charming, captivating. (see tándog).
(H) Marvellous, astounding, amazing, astonishing, wondrous, wonderful, stupendous, miraculous, extraordinary, phenomenal. (see tanhágà).
Thrice, three times. (tátlo).
(H) Exciting sleep, sleepy, lulling, drowsy, soporiferous, soporific, slumbrous, somniferous, somnific. (tuyó).

A kind of roughly made boots and shoes of Chinese manufacture from Macao; roughly made (but strong and durable). Makáw nga trabáho. Rough work, not well made. Sapátos nga makáw. Boots from Macao, boots that are not well made.

A kind of skin-disease somewhat similar to measles, but usually passing off in a few days. Also used as a verb. Ginamakáyhà siá. He has the skin-disease makáyhà. Minakáyhà siá sang isá ka túig. Last year he had the skin-disease makáyhà. Andam ka, agúd índì ka pagmakayhaón. Be careful not to catch the skin-disease makáyhà.
Nervous, etc. See makilibúton, makinugmáton).
See maki-. These two prefixes have the same meaning and may be used promiscuously. Custom and euphony decide which of the two is to be employed in any particular case.
Peaceful, peaceable, pacific, quiet, meek, loving peace and quiet, wishing to live in peace with everybody. (see dáit).
Conversationalist, orator; loving to talk or speak, addicted to-, given to-(public) speaking.
Fornicator, lewd, unchaste, wanton, lecherous, lustful, sensual, carnal, erotic, immoral, attached or addicted to sensual pleasures, inclined to sins of the flesh. (see láwas, hiláwas).
Beggar, mendicant, poor fellow. (see limós, póbre, próbe, ímol).
Also: one who is afraid of, and sees, ghosts everywhere (kítà).
Seeing well, having good eyes, sharp or keen of sight, hawk-eyed, lynx-eyed. (see kítà).
See makilitán-on.
Attached to one's own, hence: nationalistic, independent. (see kaugalíngon, makiugalíngon, makiangáyon--democratic; makihariánon--imperialistic).
Parsimonious, frugal, thrifty, sparing, saving, economic, economical, economous, spending little. (see kínì).
(Sp. maquinista) Machinist, mechanician, mechanic. (see inhenyéro).
See makínot.
Shy, bashful, avoiding the society of men. (see kuyáw).
See makinaugalíngon, makinaugalingón-nationalistic, independent, etc.

To strike, beat, smite, slap, smack, spank, thwack, whack, cudgel, thrash. Ginmakmakán akó níya sang biní-al. He beat me with a piece of split bamboo. Makmakí siá sang sinílas. Spank him with the slippers. Imákmak sa íya ang bilogón, bulunál, lalámpus, etc. Beat him with the rod, the whip, the stick, etc. (see búnal, hánot, hámpak, bálbal, lámpus, lámba, pókpok, pakáng, núsnus).
A kind of mushroom. See amamákol.

To blaze up, begin to burn well after having been kindled, to flame, flare up, burn well, said of fuel (and metaphorically of passions, or the like). Nagamákot na balá ang daíg mo? Is the fire you lighted (lit) burning well? Indì mo pagtandugón ang gatóng, kay walâ pa magmákot ang kaláyo. Don't shift the firewood, for the fire is not yet burning well. Pamakóta ang kaláyo. Let the fire burn well. Wait till the fire burns well. Pamakóti ang kaláyo. Make the fire burn brightly (by putting some kindling material, as shavings, straw, etc. on it). (see haráhará).
(H) Timid, shy, bashful, timorous, nervous. (see kúlbà).
See makutíkutí.
Bustling, stirring, hustling, pushing, a busybody; curious, prying, inquisitive. (see kutíkutí).
(B) Adult, of age, grown-up. (see mál-it, hámtong, tigúlang).
From malá-dry, etc. (see mád-an, málhan).

(B) Old, adult, advanced in age, frequently applied to people of about sixty years of age. (see mál-am). Also used as a verb. Nagmál-it siá. He has become old. Namal-itán akó sa íya. I consider him old. N.B. Mál-it is often used in contempt. Mál-it nga táo (babáe). An old fogey (hag).
(B) See mál-am, mál-it, málmal.
(B) Pillow, cushion. (see ulúnan).
Lukewarm, tepid, slightly warm, pleasantly warm, not hot. (see maalabáab).
Wide, broad, etc. See malápad.
Materials for chewing betelnut, including betelnut, lime, búyò-and tobacco-leaves. (see mamâ, malám-an).
To grasp, etc. See marámad, marásmas.
Tourist, traveller; emigrant, home-seeker. (see mangangályaw).

(H) Reappearing after death; to reappear or haunt after death. Si Fuláno, konó, nagmalánhig. N.N. they say, has risen from the grave or reappeared in the flesh. Ginamalanhigán, konó, ang íla baláy. Their house, it is said, is haunted by a ghost. (see maránhig, amamánhig, amaránhig).
That is to be tamed or broken in. (see mánso).
High, tall, large. Malántiog nga táo. A tall man. (see lántiog, malániog, maláyog, matáas).
Vagabond, loafer, tramp. (lá-og).
Loud, strong, far-reaching, sonorous, stentorian, resounding, noisy, ear-splitting, deafening, obstreperous (of sounds). (see laúy-láuy, malániog, sílik, sulánting, singgítan).

Trespassing, unobservant, unobserving, non-observant, lawless, unduteous, undutiful, neglecting, neglectful, heedless, failing to comply with, omitting the fulfilment of a duty or precept. (see lápas, malinapáson, malalíson).
(H) Thick, thickened, condensed, stiff, viscous, viscid, inspissated, treacly (of liquids); severe, heavy, vehement, violent (of fighting, or the like). (see lapúyut, malásaw, sugúng, masángsang).
What is to-be kneaded,-be made or pressed into dough. (see mása).
(H) Bad, wrong, evil, wicked, ill, sinful, criminal, unprincipled, vicious, depraved, malignant, malevolent, malicious, base, mean. (see láut, maláin).
(H) Ugly, forbidding, repulsive, nasty, hideous, improper, indecent, dirty, unclean, impure, immodest, unchaste, obscene, foul, lewd, pornographic. (see láw-ay, mahígkò, kadû).
Long, etc. See maláwig.
Conjecturable, what is to-, can-, should-, be guessed. (see máy-om).
Dim. of malayáng-wide, spacious.
(Sp. malvavisco) The marsh-mallow.
(Sp. malva) Mallow.
(Sp. maldición) Malediction, imprecation, execration, curse, malison. (see panghimaláut).

(Sp. maldita, -o) Accursed, cursed, damned; to curse, damn, imprecate, wish evil upon. Ginsilíng (Gintawág) níya akó nga maldíta. He called me accursed. (see gátud, tinagudilían, panóloy, panghimaláut, maldisyón).
(Sp. maleta) Valise, handbag, suitcase, portmanteau, grip, bag.

(B) Advantage, benefit, profit; good, well; maybe, perhaps. Warâ ti málhas kon ikáw ang silótan tungúd kang salâ ni Fuláno. It's bad enough, if you should be punished for the fault of N.N. (Literally: There is no advantage in it, if-). Warâ ti málhas kon índì tána magabút. Perhaps he is not coming. It would be too bad, if he were not coming. Indì ikáw magpanúgid nga nagasugál kamí adláwdlaw; bokón ti (warâ ti) málhas kon idakúp (dákpon) támon kang polís. Don't tell (anybody) that we are gambling every day; it would be hard lines for us, if we were caught by the police. (see águd, agúdagúd, pulús, áyhan, torán, básì, dámlag).
In order that not, so that not, lest. (see agúd índì, agúd (nga) dílì).

Dim. and Freq. of malí. Also: to insinuate, hint at, use indirect language, enlighten another's mind by allusions, speak in parables, often practised by one who wishes to obtain a favour from another or to come to an agreement, to throw out a "polite hint" in a round-about way. Ginmalímalíhan níya kamí nga ang íya nónoy buút mangasáwa sa ámon índay. He politely insinuated that his son wants to marry our daughter. Malímalíha ang paghámbal mo sa íla. Talk to them with polite insinuations or allusions. Nagamalímáli silá nga buút magsímpon sa ámon sang íla anák. They are insinuating their desire or wish of having their boy stay with us. Masúnsun ang hámbal sang Aton Ginúo malímáli. Our Lord often spoke in parables.
See malibúg.
(Sp. maligno) Malign, malignant, wicked, evil, perverse. Ang espiritú nga malígno. The devil. (see maláut).
Short, brief (particularly in the plural). (see malíp-ot).
Swift, quick, agile, nimble, lithe (of movements). (see lígsi, madásig, mapágsi).
Forbidding, abstaining from, having an objection to. (see lihî, mainumúron).
Portentous, dangerous, difficult (of times, places, situations, etc.). (see maríit).
Secretive, concealing, keeping the truth from, doing something on the sly. (see likúm).
Nervous, excited, irritable, easily upset or flurried. (see libúg).
(H) See malímbong.
(H) Forgetful, absent-minded, unmindful, oblivious. (see límot, malipáton).
(H) Overbearing, excessive, extreme, abusive, one who over-steps the bounds or does something to excess; radical. (see lakás).
Hopeful, confident, sanguine, full of expectation. (see láum).
A large rice-container of woven bamboo, capable of holding as much as thirty bushels or even more, but mostly of a size to hold about ten bushels.
Changeable, variable, fickle, not-steady,-reliable,-firm; retracting, repenting. (see liwán).
Full-grown, grown-up, strong; to become full-grown. Málmal siá nga táo. He is a full-grown man. Nagmálmal na siá. He is now full-grown. (see dakû, hámtong, hánggud).
(Sp. malo) Bad, wicked, evil. (see maláin, maláut).
Rice-flower; to flower (of rice). (see marô).
Merciful, compassionate, pitiful, having pity on, condoling, commiserating. (ló-oy).

(B) See pamulúng-to stare or gape at with open mouth (in disappointment, failure, or the like). Namalóng akó, kay walâ akó makadayón pakádto sa Ilóngílong. I am (was) greatly disappointed, because, after all, I could not go to Iloilo (as intended). Namalóng akó, kay walâ akó makatámbong dídto tungúd sang madámol nga ulán. I was sorely disappointed (I could go and whistle for it), because the heavy shower of rain prevented me from being present there. (see gamón).
See malúgus. Also: oppressing, harsh, cruel, tyrannical.
(H) See malolô.
(H) Liking, desirous of, pleased with. (lúyag; maluyagón id.).
See malúpig.
Itch, pain; to itch, hurt, pain (of a healing wound).
See malús-aw.
(H) Fond of, liking, having a liking or passion for, desirous of, etc. See maluluyagón id.
(B) For malúyag from lúyag-to like.
For mamaón from mamâ-to chew betelnut.
(B) To chew betel-nut; betel-nut chewing. Malúyag ka magmamâ? Do you like to chew betel-nut?

(B) To flatten, make flat (by pressure or by pounding), to crush or beat flat. Mamáa (lubáka, báyha) ang ságing, kay láktan ko sing kalámay. Pound the bananas soft (flat), for I am going to mix them with sugar. Mamái siá sing búnga, kay índì siá makadulút. Crush the betel-nut for him, for he is unable to bite it through. Imámà akó ánay siníng mga ságing nga tinanók. Please pound these boiled bananas for me. (lumâ, pusâ, lúbak, bayó).
Old man, father.
(Sp. mamador) The nipple of a baby's feeding bottle; nursing bottle; instrument to draw off milk. (see beberón, lulutgútan).
Dim. of mamahî. Rather well developed, not much torn or fissured, pretty well, etc.
Mortal, subject to death. (see patáy, palátyon, namátyan).
A kind of shrub with clusters of flowers and berries.
Seller, merchant, vender. (see balígyà).
Bogey, imp, sprite, goblin, elf, hobgoblin, bad fairy, wicked spirit; scarecrow; phantom. (see báhoy, pamáhoy).
Lying in wait for, ambushing, waylaying; robber, brigand. (see bángan).
Saviour, redeemer, liberator. (see báwì).
A ghost, shade, spectre, disembodied spirit, apparition, wraith, soul appearing after death, etc. See malánhig.
Publisher, reporter, journalist, publicity agent, disseminator of news, correspondent, (see bantálà).
Elf, goblin, sprite, fairy, ghost, etc. (see mamamáhoy, tamáo, tumáo, kamâkamâ, etc.).
(Sp. mameluco) Mameluke; dolt, simpleton; half-breed; a kind of rompers or underwear for small children.
One who chooses or selects something; voter, elector. (see pílì, pamílì, pumilílì, palapilián, piniliáy).
One peso each, a peso for each. Nabayáran ko silá sing mamísos ang inádlaw. I paid them each a peso a day. Mamísos karón ang kílo sang kapé. A kilo of coffee costs one peso now. (see písos).

(B) A contr. of mamun-á-from munâ-to tarry, loiter, remain a long time, protract one's stay; to be at ease, be calm or tranquil. Indì ka mámnà dídto. Don't stay there a long time, don't loiter there. Indì gid mámnà ang íya hunâhúnà túbtub nga masayóran níya kon nakadángat na sa Manílà ang íya anák nga bág-o pa lang magsakáy. She cannot rest at ease till she knows whether her son, who a short while ago embarked for Manila, has safely arrived there. (see munâ, dúgay, lúsgò).
(Sp. mamon) Cake, tart, sweet bread, sponge-cake.
A kind of fish of a considerable size and much esteemed as food.
A workman, peasant, hind, yokel, unskilled or agricultural labourer, farm-hand. (see pógon, púgon, hornaléro).
One who washes clothes; washerwoman, laundress, washerman, laundry-man. (see búnak, labandéra).
Decorator, embellisher, adorner. (see puní).
Stabber, slayer, killer, murderer, gangster, thug, assassin, cut-throat. (see bunô).
A constellation, a cluster of stars.

Also, too, as well as; well! now! Look here! Nagupúd man ikáw sa íya? Did you also accompany him? Siá malúyag magkádto man. He would like to go too. Man, nagsilíng akó sa ímo nga--. Now, look here, I told you that--. Quite frequently "man" seems to be employed as a mere decorative particle, e.g. Daw alóla man lang inâ sa ímo. That is only a trifling matter for you. Kon amó man lang ang ákon pangabúhì dirí, maáyo pa nga mapaúlì akó sa ákon bánwa. If my life here is to be only this, it would be better for me to return to my home-town. Kon sa isá man ka bágay matúod inâ--. If on the one hand-or-in one respect that is true--. Amó man gihápon. The same as ever, no change or variation, matters stand as before.
(B) See panghimál-i, kalibutáni id. Man-ihí ko kará. How can I know it. I know nothing about it. (see máan).
Snake, serpent, viper. (see sawá).
To call the dog, call the dogs together. (see tókoy, panókoy).
To benumb, cause numbness by a blow or knock. Namán-ol ang síko ko, kay nakasúnggò akó sa díngding. My elbow was benumbed, for I knocked it against the wall.
(B) He says (said) or thinks (thought). (see silíng, níya).
(Sp. maná) Manna.
Rather well-to-do, neither rich nor poor, satisfactory, sufficient. (see dawâdawâ, hingánhingán, dirâdirâ).
Fisher, fisherman. (see panágat, mangingísdà).
Pouncing upon like birds of prey, grabbing, tearing to pieces (as a bird of prey does). Píspis nga mananágit. A bird of prey. (see dágit).
Prophet. (see manalágnà). (tágnà-lágnà).
Tailor, seamstress. (see tahî)
Usurper, transgressor, encroacher. (see sáklam).
Eye-witness, spectator, onlooker. (see tán-aw).
Domestic animals; meat of animals that live and breed on land.
The vocative of mánang.
Toddy-gatherer, tubâ-collector, one whose daily business is to climb a number of coconut palms and to collect the palm-wine. (see tubéro-a seller of, dealer in, tubá).
A kind of bird of prey; a hawk.
See manaól.
(H) Familiarly used for mánang-eldest sister.
Victor, conqueror, winner; victorious, triumphant. (see daúg).

(B) (Sp. mandato) Order, command, mandate, injunction, regulation, precept; leader; ringleader, originator, one who starts or is chiefly responsible for an act. Ikáw gid ang mandátos sinâ. It was you who started that. You are the one who is responsible for that. (see sógò, kasogoán, pangúlo, manugpahítò, kábo, manugdumála).
Aunt; stepmother, foster-mother; dear old woman. (see tíà, tíyà, darâ, áling, bóboy).

(Sp. mandar) To rule, guide, direct, govern, sway, regulate, control, have authority over, hold sway, command, lead. Iámpò ta nga mandoán sang Diós si N.N. sa pagdumála sa áton sing maáyo. Let us pray to God that he may direct N.N. so that he may govern us well. Sín-o ang nagamándò? Who is in charge? Who commands or rules? (see gahúm, dumála, pasunúd, sógò, buót).
(Sp. mando) Authority, office, power, sway, rule, command. (see gahúm, palangakóan, dumála, batúta).
See manghátì, manghatión-twenty-five centavos each, etc. (see kahátì).
Tourist, sight-seer, traveller; emigrant, home-seeker, one who goes to live or moves to another place. (see malangályaw, mangangáyaw, pangáyaw).
(H) Reaper, harvester, one who reaps rice by means of a "kayóg". (see áni, manganganí, manuganí).
Reaper, harvester. See mangalaní.
Eater, feaster. (see káon).
Helper, supporter, assistant, second, upholder, protector. (see ápin, umalapín).
A representative, delegate, senator; proxy, one who presents himself or confronts a situation. (see atúbang, tigpangatubáng).
Thief, etc. See makáwtì, makáwat.
Stranger, foreigner, sojourner, tourist, traveller. See mangalályaw, etc.
(Sp. manga) Sleeve. (see pakô, pákpak, sóol).
(Sp. mango) The mango-tree and its fruit. (see páhò).

Riches, possessions, property, wealth, assets, capital; to become rich, acquire property, etc. Ang kalabánan sang mga táo nagapaningúhà magmánggad. The majority of men strive to become rich. Nagmánggad siá sa íla nga palatikángan. He got rich in their business. (see pagkabutáng).
Rich, etc. See manggáran. (see pilákan, bangkílan, aligyanán).
(Sp. mango) Penholder, handle, helve, haft (of tools, etc.). (see ápal, kaláptan, pólo, uluyatán).
Trouble-maker, rowdy, gangster, turbulent fellow, ruffian, riotous, revolutionary, disturbing the peace. (see gúbat, huróng, manriríbok, magamó).
To arrange, put in order, sort, assort, classify, manage well. (Perhaps from the Sp. manejar). Manghará ang baráha mo. Arrange your cards in order according to their suits. (see kaláging, húsay).
(B) Merciful, compassionate, feeling for, commiserative, condoletory, ruthful, pitiful, etc. See malolóy-on. (see ngír-o).
One who judges, a judge, justice. (see hokóm, panghokóm).
A younger brother or sister; not of age, minor; not ripe, unripe, immature, green (of fruits). (see libáyon, kalibáynan, línghod).
Considerate, thoughtful, careful, solicitous; attentive, mindful, heedful, regardful. (see ngílin).
A verbal form of panginbabáe, panginbabáye, but sometimes used as an adjective like palanginbabáe-addicted to women, etc.
One who eats raw meat, etc.; a cannibal. (see kílaw).
A shell-gatherer, collector of sea-shells; grabber, grafter, boodler. (see pangínhas, pakinháson).
(B) Merciful. See manghír-óhon id. (ngír-o).
(B) Compassionate, merciful. See manghir-óhon.
(B) Jack tree and jack fruit. (see lángkà id.).
A kind of hardwood tree and its valuable timber.
One who walks on foot, a footman, foot-soldier, infantry-man; infantry. (see lakát).
Rich, having plenty of money. (see mángmang, pilákan, manggáran, manggaránon, bankílan, aligyanán).
Dull, stupid, brainless; an ass, fool. (see tipangág, pangág, pángog, balingág, balingá, búngaw, tampuháw, búang, kólò).
Brave, courageous, fearless, reliable, trustworthy, fierce. Mángtas nga idô. A good watchdog. (see mántas).
A charcoal-burner, charcoal-man. (see úling).
Farmer, tiller of the soil, agricultural labourer. (see umá).
(Sp. mangostán) Mangosteen.
(Sp. maní) Peanut, earthnut, groundnut, goober.
Ticklish, irritating, having a creepy or ticklish feeling, easily tickled; nervous, excited. (see hilás).
(B) Tingling, grating, squeaking, sharp, gritty, setting one's teeth on edge, said of sensations, etc. (see nílo, mangílo, mangiló).
Godmother. (see padríno, panínoy-godfather; madrína).
Agonizing, in one's last agony, on one's death bed. (see tingâ).
Docile, obedient, submissive, submitting, yielding, dutiful, but mostly used in the negative form dìmanínggol-stubborn, disobedient, headstrong, obdurate, intractable. (see tínggol, panínggol).
A potter, one who makes or sells earthenware vessels; manufacturing, industrial. (see díhon).
Watchful, observing, observant, prying, spying; spy, detective, sleuth. Polís nga maniniíd. Secret service man. Detective. (see tíid, maninilág, tíktik, lampitáw).
A thief; pilfering, thievish. (tíkas).
Thief, petty thief, pilferer, sneak. (see tíkmà, maniníkas).
An observer, spy. (panílag).
A kind of a dark-coloured snake growing to a considerable size and very harmful to chickens, eggs, etc., but non-poisonous.
Setting fire to, an incendiary, one who commits arson. (see síndot).
A listener, eavesdropper, one who overhears a conversation, a spy. (see tingád).
See mángkà-jackfruit.
A kind of large-eyed (broad-eyed) frog; vermin; a wild boar or pig; wild beasts in general.
Revolutionary, riotous, mutinous, agitator, exciting a commotion or tumult. (see ribók).
A kind of small octopus. (see kugíta-a large octopus).
A large sea shell.
One who (that which) unbinds, solves, opens, explains or translates something. Manlulúbad sang hámbal. An interpreter. (see lubád).
Flyer, aviator; winged. (see lupád).

A contraction of manungâ. Also: middle-aged, from about thirty-five to fifty-five years of age. Daw anó kamál-am (katigúlang) si Fuláno?-Mánngà (siá). How old is N.N.?-He is middle-aged. (see médya, bída).
Dim. of manobô. Rather low, rather short, of low stature, a little less than normal in height. Maníwang siá kag manobônóbò. He was lean and rather low in stature.

A prefix denoting occupation with what the root or term implies to which it is attached, e.g. manogarádo-a plougher; manogdumúg-a wrestler; manoghábul-a weaver; manoglála-a basket-weaver, one who makes wickerwork; manogabút-one about, or expected, to arrive; manogkádto-one about to leave or go somewhere, manogtapús-one about to finish or complete (his studies, a job, etc.). N.B. Very frequently the prefix manog-produces a shifting of the accent of the term to which it is attached, e.g. manogdumúg (dúmug); manoghábul (habúl); manogtapús (tápus) and many more. (manug-id.).
An object played from the hand in various games, as a ball, stone, marble, card, etc. (see máno).
Low, mean, boorish, uncultured, very common, rough, coarse, rude, vulgar, not fit or proper for educated or refined people. (see bástos).
The eldest brother. (see mánang-the eldest sister).
(H) Eldest brother (familiar). (see mánong, manóng).
(Sp. mancha) Stain, blotch, blur, taint, spot, blot, blemish, dirt. (see dágtà, bulíng, hígkò, etc.).
(Sp. manzanilla) The common chamomile, a medicinal plant.
See amansebádo-one living in concubinage.
Nurse, wet-nurse, children's nurse. (see yáya, sisiwá).
(English: manchester) White cotton cloth, twill, drill, Manchester goods or wares.
(Sp. manso) Tame, domestic, domesticated, gentle, meek, willing, broken in, well trained, subdued, tractable. (see mahagúp, mabúot, antâ).
Reliable, etc. (of watch-dogs). See mángtas id.
(Sp. manteca) Lard, fat, dripping. (see támbok).
(Sp. mantequilla) Butter.
(Sp. mantel) Table-cloth, altar-cloth, table-cover. (see tabón).
(Sp. mantellina) Mantilla, a woman's head-shawl, woman's veil. (see kúnop, kúmbung, takuróng, tákdong, kúdong).

(Sp. mantener) To maintain, keep up, hold out, support, keep alive, manage to go on. Nagamantenér gid lang silá sang íla pangabúhì. They are just managing to keep alive, they are supporting themselves rather poorly or with difficulty. Mantenehón mo ánay ang kalát, kay kuháon ko pa ang tigíb. Hold the rope in position, for I am going to fetch the chisel. Komústa kamó?-Nagamantenér kamí. How are you?-We are getting along pretty well. Nagaduhádúha akó kon makamantenér siá dídto sing maláwig nga tión. I wonder (doubt), whether he will be able to support himself there (remain there) for any length of time. Mantenér lang. It will do-for the present,-to go on with. It is only-a make-shift,-a temporary substitute, or the like.
A ghost. See mantíw.
Bewitched, charmed, wonderful. (see mantíw).
A bugbear, a ghost supposed to be of gigantic proportions and of terrible aspect; jinnee, jinn.
Bewitched, etc. See mantihón.
(Sp. manto) A head-covering, head-shawl (for women). (see mantelyína).
A ghost. See mantíw.
See manog-.
Butcher, slaughterer, dealer in meat. (see íhaw).
One who is an adept at working various designs into cloth. An expert in arranging and adapting the thread of the warp for making multicoloured designs. (see bibít).
A singer of Christmas carols. (see daígon).
Governor, director, administrator, manager, ruler, boss. (dumála).
An expert in removing foreign bodies from the eye, eye-cleaner, oculist. (see gáhid).
Masseur, masseuse, one who practises massage. (see hílot).
A palmister, fortune-teller, chiromancer, one who practises palmistry. (see pálad, himálad).
A sawyer, one who saws wood. (see lagárì).
One who pushes or presses forward. Manugsiúg sang tigbató. A type-setter. (see síug).
Author, writer, a literary man. (see sulát, magsusúlat, manunúlat).
Investigator, inspector, examiner. Manugsusipuód. Manugsusipuodnanon. Provincial Inspector. (see súsi).
Tailor, cutter. (see tábas, sástre).
Messenger; angel. (see manunúndà, manugtúndà, anhél).
(Probably from the Sp. tumbar) A stunner, surprising, amazing, overwhelming, overpowering.
A farmer, tiller of the soil, peasant; rustic, rude, uncultured. (see umá, umánhon).
A kind of vine whose bitter juice is used as an antiseptic in cleaning wounds, etc.
Guide, leader. (see tóytoy).
A disturber; disturbing, interrupting, interfering with, causing a disturbance. (see túblag).
An unwelcome visitor, a parasite, sycophant. (see panudángsudáng).
Teacher, etc. See manunúon, maéstro. (see túdlò, panúdlo).
Seer, prophet, propounder of riddles, riddle maker, riddle solver; wise, sage. (see túgma).
A writer, author. See magsusúlat, manugsúlat.
Accuser, plaintiff. Manunúmbung puodnánon. Provincial Fiscal. (see súmbung).
Teacher, professor, master, tutor, instructor. (see toón, magtotóon, magtutúon).
Plotter, gangster, murderer, conspirator, one who intends to harm, or to wreak vengeance upon, others. (see tuyô).
To go on well, prosper, make progress, be well-to-do. (see manháwà).

(B) Greedy, voracious, ravenous, wolfish, gluttonous. The verb is minaóg-to be greedy, eat greedily. Maóg siá nga táo. He is a greedy man. He is a voracious eater. Indì ka magminaóg. Don't be greedy. (see hákug, dalók, dinalók).

(Sp. mapa) A map, plan, drawing, topographic outline; to map, map out, make a map. Mapáha iníng papél. Use this paper to draw a plan on. Mapáhi ang ákon dútà. Make a map of my lands. Mapáhi akó sang ákon talámnan. Make me a map of my fields. Buás ugáling pagasóklon kag pagamapáhan ko ang ímo nga dútà. Not just now, but to-morrow I will measure your grounds and draw a map of them.
Negligent, careless, letting things take their course without any serious reflection or effort at remedying the state of affairs, putting off, procrastinating, (see pabuyánbúyan).
(H) Amenable to persuasion or bribery, easily led, easily won over by argument or bribes. (dalá).
One easily swayed or carried along, not steadfast, not firm of character, unreliable, vacillating. (see dalá, padalá).
Open, frank, candid, plain spoken. (see paháyag).
Patient, meek, tolerant, submissive, resigned, gentle, long-suffering, bearing with. (see paílub).
See the following mapainubúson.
See mapailúbon.
Generous, liberal, munificent, free, open-handed; giver, giving. (see hátag, maálwan).
(H) Circumspect, prudent, watchful, wary, chary, cautious. Ang táo nga mapanginlamánon malayô sa katalágman. A cautious man is far removed from danger. Forewarned, forearmed. (see panginláman).
See mapanghatágon.
Observant, watchful, open-eyed, alive to, awake to, vigilant, wide awake, guarded, on the lookout. (see panílag).
Credulous, gullible, easily believing any story or report, easily taken in. (páti).
Prolific, productive, fertile, fruitful, frugiferous, fecund, yielding a good crop. (see patubás, palatúbson).
Productive, etc. See mapinatubóon.
Considerate, thoughtful, mindful of, having regard or consideration for, conscientious. (see patugsíling).
Negligent, careless, dilatory, procrastinating. (see patumbáyà).
Negligent, unconcerned, careless, heedless. (patumbáya; see mapabuyánbuyánon).
Selfish, egoistic, pleasing oneself, self-indulgent, worldly-minded. (see patúyang).
Humble, etc. See mapainubúson, mapainubsánon.
Harsh, etc. See mapígus, malupígon.
Insisting, persistent, urging, pressing, importunate; sticking to. (see pílit, pilít).
Lasting, enduring, permanent, constant, persevering. (see dáyon).
Obliging, pleasing, considerate, thoughtful, ingratiating, tactful, regardful. (see buút, hamúot, pahamúot).
Doting, petting, caressing, fondling, cherishing, kind, kindly, tender, affectionate. (see palánggà).
Devout, pious, a man of prayer. (see pangadî).
Mindful, regardful. Dílì (dî) mapinasapayánon-indifferent, careless, thoughtless. (see sapayán, waláy, sapayán, pagkadilìmapinasapayanón).
Insulting, affronting, deriding, mocking, scoffing, blaspheming, blasphemous, scurrilous, gibing, abusive, jeering, vilifying. (see pasipála).
Credulous, gullible, unsuspecting, easily deceived or tricked. (see páti, mapatípatíhon).
Founding, establishing, erecting, laying the foundations of, instituting; inventing, making up (a story, lie, etc.). (see pátok).
Strict, close, narrow, contracted, straitened, dense, crowded, packed, pressed together, hard-pressed; hard, difficult, severe. (see píot).
See mapúlaw. Also: Wanting little sleep, staying up long, keeping late hours, sleepless.
See mapinuslánon-useful, etc.
Dirty, ugly, nasty, abominable, sullied, soiled. (see raíng, mahígkò, maláw-ay, magím-ang, kalaímnan, marígkam, marísmò).
(B) The mole-cricket. See malámalá.
(Sp. maravilla) A kind of flowering plant, marigold; deep pink colour.
(B) Sticky, viscous, adhesive, stiff. Mabúdlay ang paglakát sa maragkót nga lalaó. Walking through sticky mud is tiresome. (see ragkót, mapilít).
Crisp, short. (see ragomó, mahágpok).
Story, history, event, incident, anecdote, chronicle, record. (see histórya).
Historical, eventful, momentous, memorable. Maragtásnon nga hitabû. An historical event. Maragtásnon nga túig. An eventful year.
The male of the singgálong (fox; civet cat).
(B) Liable to attract-, to become infested with-, ants called lásgà, particularly said of eatables. (see masulubáyon).

(B) To be wide awake, be fully aware of, to grasp, comprehend, understand, take in. Warâ akó kamarámad kang ginkoón na. (Walâ akó makahangúp (makamarásmas) sang ginsilíng níya). I don't (did not, didn't) understand what he says (said). Karámad kaw kará? (Makasáyod, makahibaló ka sinâ?). Can you understand it? Do you know that? (see malámad, marásmas, hibalú, sáyod, balintúnod, áto, hántup, hangúp).
(B) A ghost, spectre, etc. See malánhig.
(B) Stinking, smelling, having a bad smell, giving off a stench, of an evil or obnoxious smell or odour. (see rapúg, mabahô, mabáhò, makalolóod, makangingíl-ad).

To be wide (fully) awake, be awake to, to grasp, comprehend, understand, take in, take. Walâ siá makamarásmas sang ákon nga gin silíng. He could not understand what I said. Namarasmasán níya ang tanán nga ginpaháyag ni Fuláno. He comprehended all that N.N. expounded. Namarasmasán akó sang dídto na akó sa baláy. I recovered my senses when I got to the house. (see marámad, mádmad, hangúp, hántup, balintúnod, áto, sáyod, másngà).
(Sp. marga, margajita) Pyrites, mispickel; marl.
(B) Thick, stout, round, plump, fat of arms, calves, cheeks, etc. (ribúok). (see matibúnog, matipúlon, manipólon).
(Sp. marido) Husband. (see bána).
Hot, sultry, stuffy, sweltry, close; disturbed, upset, perplexed, confused, excited through overwork or through having too many things to attend to. (rigáhot). (see magín-ot, mabóhot, gomón).
Haunted, weird, dreary, desolate, depressing, lonely, lonesome, inspiring fear, uncanny, said particularly of lonely places. (see ríit).
Complicated, mingled, combined, confused, involved. (rikót). (see gomón). Marikót nga pangabúdlay. Complicated work that requires great patience, etc.
(B) Dim. of marímis. Rather sweet, sweetish.
(B) Sweet, sugary, syrupy. (see rímis, matám-is, dólse).
(Sp. marques, marquesa) Marquis, marquess; marchioness, marquise.
(Sp. marmol) Marble. Batungdáan nga mármol (bukáy). A marble monument. (see bató, nga, bukáy).
(B) Wild, untamed. (see simarón id.).
(Sp. marfil) Ivory.
(Sp. Marzo) March. (see dagangbúlan).
(Sp. Martes) Tuesday.
(Sp. martillo) Hammer, mallet. (see palapâ, palô).
(Sp. martir) Martyr. (see tigbatás).
(B) The East. (see murúd-an, sidlangán).
(H) Ever. Dílì nga más-a-never. (see mugís).
(H) To waste, squander, throw away, spend to no purpose. (see kamásà, uyáng, úsik, pilák).
(Sp. masa) Dough, mass, lump; to knead. Masáha ang arína. Knead the flour. Masáhi akó sing isá ka sáko nga arína. Knead one sack of flour for me. (see lamás, malasahón).
(Sp. maza) The hub, nave of a wheel.
Also: Injured, spoilt, rotten, worm-eaten (of fruits). (see torakón).
Sickly, invalid, unhealthy, having poor health, inclined, or liable, to be often sick; causing pain, painful; sharp, cutting (of speech). (see masakít).
(H) Erring, mistaken, making a-mistake,-blunder,-mess of, blundering, doing a thing wrong, committing a fault or blunder. (see sayúp, masinaláypon).
Pleasing, pleasant, cheerful. (see alikáya, masádya).
To feast, attend a banquet, eat much or to one's heart's content. (see páskwa, tábad, laód, pasáy, páskon).
(Sp. maceta) Flower-pot. (see masíta).
(Sp. demasiado) Excessive, more than enough, very much, too much, overdone. (see támà, lám-ag).
See under nasig-.
A prefix denoting equality of condition, e.g. masigkatáo-a man like ourselves, a fellow-man, neighbour. (see isigka-).
Sympathetic, regardful, considerate, thoughtful, affectionate, compassionate; emotional, sentimental. (see sín-it, kasín-it).
A frequent church-goer; devout, pious, religious, a man of prayer. (see símba, simbáhan, silimbáhon, mainampóon).
Discontented, displeased, unsatisfied, grumbling on account of having received less than others, envious, spiteful. (sabít).
Cheerful, jolly, etc. See masádya. (see maluyagón).
Supporting, helpful, assisting, looking after, taking care of. (see sákdag, maampínon, mainapínon).
Sorry, sad, desolate, dismal, dejected, mournful, doleful, dolorous, distressed, dreary, sorrowful. (see subô, masubô).
Conform, conformable, agreeing, willing, ready, complying, compliant, obliging, obedient, docile, yielding. (see sugút).
See masinulúndon-obedient, etc.
See masariwáol. Masiriwáol is more in use.
(B) Dim, obscure, getting dark, fading light, twilight, crepuscular, gloaming, said of nightfall. (sirúm).
(Sp. maceta) Flower-pot. (see masetéra). Also: Plants and flowers set out in flower-pots.
(Sp. mascabado) Unrefined sugar, muscovado.
(Sp. máscara) Mask, disguise, face-mask; masquerade.
(Sp. por más que) Even if, though, although, notwithstanding. (see bisán).
To be or become aware of, know, understand. See namaslután. (see marásmas, malámad).

(B) Clear, bright, said of light or sight. Dílì másna iníng kínki, kay may bíro ang túbo. This lamp is not bright, because the chimney is sooty. Dílì na másna ang panúluk ko, kay tigúlang na man akó. My sight is getting dim, for I am quite old. (see masánag).

To know, understand. Indì siá makamásngà magbása kag magsulát. He does not know how to read and write. Walâ siá sing namasngaán nahanungúd sináng mga butáng. He hasn't an inkling of those matters. (see hibaló, balintúnod, marásmas, etc.).
(Sp. mazo) A mallet, a heavy hammer, sledge-hammer, mall, maul, beetle.
Nauseating, sickening, revolting, exciting a feeling of loathing, uninviting, unappetizing, applied especially to food cooked in too much fat. (see somó, makasolómo, mabútlà, masúm-od).
(Sp. mason) Freemason.
(Sp. masoneria) Freemasonry.
A convulsive choking fit that often attacks young children and may easily end in death, unless help is rendered at once.
See máslut-to be aware of, etc.
(H) See masagíl-om id.
Twisted, complicated, involved, entangled.
See masulukisák. (sulukusák-sulukisák).
Weak, easy to conquer or overcome. (see súpil, dalág-on, mapígaw, malúya).
Writer; correspondent (of a newspaper, etc.); author, literary man. (see sulát).
From matá. See máthan id.

Something in sight, at hand, something that turns up, ready for use, way of earning a livelihood. Walâ siá sing mát-an kag sáp-an. There is (was) nothing (no means, work, help, etc.) in sight for his need and he has (had) nowhere to go to for shelter or protection. (see matá, palangitán-an, paaliwánsan, dalángpan, aláypan, pangítà).
(B) Family, blood relation. (see bátà, himatâ).
Proud, self-conscious, insolent, haughty, overbearing, arrogant, bumptious, stuck-up, supercilious, overweening. (táas).
A kind of banana similar to kadísnon and anonóo and eaten either raw or boiled.
Straight, straight-forward, direct, right, rectilinear, honest, frank. (tádlung).
Grateful, thankful, mindful of, making a proper return for favours received. (see bálus, matinagubalúson).
(B) Pilfering, stealing. (see takáb, maniníkas, makáwat, matákaw).
Apathetic, etc. See matinalák-on.
Marking, noting, taking stock, observing well, taking note of or paying much attention to. (see tándà, matinandáon).
Wonderful, miraculous, extraordinary, marvellous, strange, surprising, astonishing; one who wonders or is surprised. (see tanhágà, makatitingála, makatalanhágà).
(Sp. matanza) Slaughter; license to slaughter animals; payment for the license to slaughter animals. (see íhaw, ilihawán).
Easily broken, breakable, flimsy, fragile, weak, worn-out, brittle, frail. (see tapúk).
Coward, etc. See matálaw.
Plump, thick, fat, stout, fleshy, round, chubby, rosy, peachy (of cheeks, etc.; see matípsul, matibúnog, etc.).
News, information, notice. (see balítà).

To listen in, hear, get notice of, receive news, eavesdrop. Nakamatík ka nga may mga buyóng nga magaabút? Have you heard that there are brigands (gangsters) approaching? Walâ akó sing namatikán sang íla sugilánon. I could not (did not) understand what they were talking about. (see mutík).
Revengeful, vindictive, vengeful, brooding over, resentful, retaliating, desirous of giving tit for tat, harbouring vengeance. (see timalús, bálus).
(B) Round, spherical, orbicular, globular, circular. (see timbúlog, manipólon, matibúnog, matipúlon).
Affable, kind, amiable, courteous, humane, sociable. (see támyaw, mainabláwon, mabugnóhon).

Dirtying, soiling, staining, stainful. Ang íya nga ginhámbal matinap-íngon gid sang kadunggánan ni Fuláno. His speech cast a slur on (was detrimental to) N.N.'s reputation (honour, character). (see táp-ing).

Conscientious, administering or managing with care, being in charge of or responsible for, looking after with great care, mindful, thoughtful, circumspect. (see tátap, mainandámon, mainamlígon, mapísan, maúkud, matútum).
Active, energetic, strenuous, assiduous, doing one's best, striving hard, making great efforts. (see tingúhà).
Preserving well, hiding away, guarding, saving, shutting up, putting by, keeping, looking after with care, lest things should be spoilt, lost or stolen. (see típig).
Faithful, believer, follower. (see tóo).
Disturbing, upsetting, interfering with. (see túblag).
Redeeming, reclaiming, saving, liberating, freeing. (see tubús, manunúbus).
Complying with, compliant, obedient to, observant, prompt to obey, dutiful, fulfilling one's duties, disciplined, executing orders received. (see túman, masinulúndon, masinulúgton).
Soluble, dissolving, melting. (see túnaw).
True, sincere, honest, frank, loving truth and honesty. (see túud, matúud).
Decided, determined, resolute, firm, purposeful, having made up one's mind. (see túyò).
Directing, pointing out the way, guiding, leading. (see tóytoy).

Ulceration, suppuration, festering, infection, sepsis; to fester, suppurate, mortify, gangrene, gather pus or matter, rankle; to throb, pulsate, palpitate (of ulcers and boils). Nagamatitík ang íya hubág. His ulcer suppurates or gathers pus. Nagmatitík ang nánà sa sulúd sang pilás sa pagpangíta sing lútsan pa gwâ. The pus inside the wound began to throb seeking an outlet. (see pitík, patík).

To do something by degrees, step by step, gradually, piecemeal, in slow but sure stages, do slowly, deliberately. Nagamátmat sa pagdakû iníng tanúm. This plant is growing tall by slow degrees. Ginmátmat níya ang kúhà (ang pagkúhà) sang íya nga galamitón sa baláy ni Fuláno. He took away his furniture from N.N.'s house one by one or piece by piece. Matmatá sang arádo ang ímo umá. Plough your field leisurely or in easy stages. Ang kaámyon sang mga búlak nagamátmat guób (sa pagguób) sang mga talámnan. The fragrance of the flowers is slowly spreading over the fields. (see amát, amátamát).
(Sp. matrero) Cunning, tricky, tricksy, knavish, mean, cheating; rogue, sneak, cheat. (see agóng, lág-it, antígo).
(Sp. machihembrar) Dovetailed, tongued and grooved; to dovetail, tenon, tongue and groove.
(Sp. machorra) An old barren cow; a cow that does not bear any longer and is being fattened for slaughter.
Determined, fixed, clear, not equivocal or ambiguous, not involved (of a word or sentence); spinning, turning, revolving. (see matúrong).
Sleepy, drowsy, nodding. (see tuyó, matuyó, matuyohón).
Dewy, full of dew, dew-drenched, roral, roric, roscid. (see tún-og).
Angry, irritable, very impatient, irascible, bad-tempered, choleric, touchy, techy; annoying, harassing, provoking. (see úgtas, maúgtas, makaulúgtas).
(H) Rainy, wet, showery. Ang maulánon nga panahón. The wet (rainy) season. (see ulán).
(H) Mindful of, concerned about, thinking of, cherishing. (see ulikíd, mabinalíkdon, maulínggon).
A kind of rough cloth. Sárwal nga maúng. Trousers made of rough cloth. A pair of rough trousers.
See maúpang.
Progressive, making-progress,-headway, going ahead, forging ahead, prosperous, getting on, going on well. (see úswag, mainuswagón).
Plentiful, galore, abundant; fertile, good, productive (of soil). (see úya, mapinatubóon).

Unlucky, unhappy, liable to be interfered with, particularly said of families, one of whose members met death by drowning. A superstitious belief has it, that it will always be either rainy or stormy, whenever such a family gets up some merry-making, as at a marriage, baptism, picnic, etc. (see úyaw).
Wide, broad, large, extensive, spacious, vast, ample. (see wayáng, mahanáhay, malápad).

Liking, pleased with, taking pleasure in, devoted to, inclined to, addicted to, partial to, gone on. Mawilíhon siá sang síne, sang mga palagwáon, etc. He likes to go to moving picture shows, is partial to theatres or stage-plays, etc. Mawilíhon siá sang sa sulúd sang baláy kag matinalákon sang mga pangalípay sa luás sang baláy. She loves her home and is averse to pleasures outside her home. (see wíli, maluyagón).

An evil spirit, bogy, bogey, goblin, hobgoblin, bugbear, bugaboo, a mischievous ghost. Karón ipadakúp ko ikáw sa máwmaw. Now I shall hand you over to the máwmaw. Halá, ára na dirâ ang máwmaw. Look out, the máwmaw is over there. (see mámaw; N.B. These terms are often used to intimidate or threaten disobedient children).
Long, robust, strong (of limbs, etc.). (see maláwhan).
(Sp. máxima) Axiom, maxim, apothegm, sentence, saying, saw, proverb, thought. (see hurubáton, hinun-ánon).
(Sp. maximum) The maximum, the extreme limit, the utmost, uttermost. (dìmalabihán).

There is or exists; to have. May ulán. There is rain. It rains. May lángit kag inpiérno. There is a heaven and a hell. Heaven and hell exist. May kwárta siá. He has money. May baláy siá nga kaugalíngon. He has a house of his own. May ginabátyag siá. He has a feeling of sickness. He feels sick. May duhá siá ka útud. He has two brothers. Malúyag akó nga may áwto akó. I should like to have (own, possess) an automobile. Sa may káhoy--. There where the tree stands--. Sa may pílak mahulás iní. This is easy for one who has money. Sa may upúd siá ukón sa walâ--. Whether he has a companion or no--. At all events, whether with, or without, a companion--. Sa may ulán kag sa may ínit--. In rain or (and) shine--. Kon may pílak lang akó--. If I only had (the) money--. Sang may mánggad pa akó--. When I was still wealthy (rich)--. Sa may lúyag ikáw ukón (kag) sa walâ--. Whether you like or not (nolens volens)--. (see walá-no, none, there is not, does not exist).
To guess, etc. See mái-om. Mahapús may-omón nga--. It is easy to guess that--.
Sack, bag. (see bayóong, mái-ong).
A kind of bird, somewhat like a sparrow.
A fish much esteemed as food.
A kind of mushroom.
A kind of maya-bird.
A kind of song-bird.
Flat, plain (of face, etc.). (see kuyámpad).
(Sp. mayordomo) Steward, butler, superintendent or manager of a household, etc. (see manugtátap, manugdumála).
Smiling, with a pleasant face, with a face radiant with good cheer, gay, gladsome, joyous, cheerful. (see yuhúm).
Soft, tender, mild, yielding, impressible, impressionable, malleable. (see yúm-ok, malúm-ok, maramî, mayamî).
(Sp. mayúscula) Capital letter, upper-case letter. (see minúskula-small letter).
(Sp. medalla) Medal, plaque.
(Sp. medallon) A large medal, locket, medallion.
(Sp. medida) Measure, foot-rule, yard-measure, measurement. (see takús, taláksan).
(Sp. médico) Doctor, physician, medical man, leech. (manogbúlong).
(Sp. medicina) Medicine, physic, medicament, drug, potion, nostrum. (see bulúng).
(Sp. media) Stocking, hose; socks.
(Sp. medio) Half; means, medium, contrivance, resource, remedy. (see tungâ, kalalángan, padihútan, pahitôhítò, remédyo).
(Sp. melaza) Molasses. (see lasáw, pulút, arníbal).
(Sp. melindre) A kind of shrub with beautiful, rose-coloured flowers.
(Sp. melon) Melon. (see sandíya).
(Sp. menor) Minor; younger; a minor (in music). (see mánghud, línghod).

(Sp. menear) To move, shake, stir; to wear out, dislocate, be displaced or dislodged. Nagmenyár ang mga halígi sináng baláy tungúd sang bágyo. The posts of this house were dislodged by the storm. (see úyug, hiláy, balingíg).
(Sp. merengue) Meringue, a kind of candy; sugar plum.
(Sp. merienda) Lunch, afternoon tea, collation, snack. (see pamáhaw).
(Sp. mérito) Merit, desert, worth. (see palahanúngdan, takús).
(Sp. mercado) Market, mart, market-place. (see tiénda).
(Sp. merma) Waste, leakage, shrinkage. (see búhin, kúlpà, kupús).
(Sp. mezcla) Mixture, admixture, mingling, combination, conglomeration, jumble, hash, hotchpotch, compound, medley. (see lákay, lakót, sakót, sámò, símbug).
(Sp. metal) Metal.
(Sp. metate) A primitive corn-mill, a rounded stone for grinding maize or crushing cocoa (cacao).
(Sp. metro) Metre, (39.37 inches); metre in poetry.
About, almost, nearly. Sa mga las ótso. At about eight o'clock. Sang mga tátlo na ka búlan--. Almost or about three months ago. Kon mga saráng--. If possible, if you please--.
The sign for the plural, e.g. ang idô-the dog; ang mga idô-the dogs; iníng káhoy-this tree; iníng mga káhoy-these trees.
(Sp. mientras) While, whilst, as long as, during the time that--. Miéntras tánto. (a corruption of the Sp. entre tanto). Meanwhile. In or during the interval. (see sámtang).
(Sp. miércoles) Wednesday.
(Sp. microbio) Microbe, bacterium, bacillus. (see kágaw).
(Sp. mil) Thousand. (see líbo).
See mirâ-mirâ-rheum (from the eyes), etc.
To squeeze, compress, flatten, crush. Milimilihá ang kán-on nga natigánà sa linúgaw. Squeeze the rice for the rice-porridge. Ginamilímilí siá sa kautangán. He is crushed by debts. (see kúmus).
(S. milicia) Militia, military, soldiery; strategy, art and science of war, warfare. (see mangangawáy, áway, ináway).
(Sp. militar) Military, war-like, martial; soldier, warrior, military man. (see mangangawáy).
What is to-, should-, can-, be said or pronounced; saying, speech, utterance; to utter, say, give out. (see mítlang).
(H) Eyelash. (see amimilók).
(Sp. millon) A million. (see ramák, hámbad).
(Sp. millonario) Millionaire. (see ramákan, hambádan).
Bleating; to bleat; go to sleep, go to by-by (of children). Ang mga karnéro kag kánding nagamímì. Sheep and goats bleat. Mamímì ka na, totô? Do you want to sleep (now), darling?

Crushed, squeezed, pressed; compressed; to crush, squeeze, press, compress, destroy the natural condition or shape of a thing by pressure. Kálò nga mîmî. A crushed hat. Indì mo pagmîmión ang maléta. Don't crush (squeeze out of shape) the handbag. (see pusâ, lumâ).
To call the cat. (see kóring, koríng).

(Sp. mina) Mine; to mine, to mint. Mináha ang buláwan nga nagasímbug siníng bató. Mine the gold mixed with this rock. Ginmináhan kitá sang pangolohán sing bág-o nga pílak. The government minted for us new silver coins. (see duláng, dulángan).
(Sp. mineral) Mineral.

To be or become sad, dejected, pensive, dismal, doleful, dreary, downcast, lonesome, sentimental, cheerless, disconsolate, glum, desolate. Nagmíngaw iníng lugár, kútub sang paghalín sang mga táo. This place has become dreary since the departure of the people. Namingáwan akó dirí. I feel sad or lonely here in this place. (see subô).
(Sp. ministro) Minister; agent; subordinate.

(Sp. menos) No good, poor, mean, defective, bad, not well done or said, inferior, mediocre, below expectations, not up to the mark or standard; to grow less, deteriorate, be bad. Nagmínus ang pinatubás ko nga humáy sa karón nga túig. This year I had a poor crop of rice. (see kulabús, kabús, maláin, kúlang).
(Sp. minúscula) Small letter, lower-case letter. (see mayúskula-capital letter).

Married or wedded people, living in wedlock, joined in matrimony; to cohabit, live together as husband and wife. Walâ pa silá makasál, ápang nagamínyò na silá. They are not yet married, nevertheless they are living together already as husband and wife. (see magasawá, kasál, hilúngug).
See mirâ-mirâ, which is more commonly used.
An exudation from the eyes, rheum, a flow of mucus from the eyes; to flow from the eyes (as mucus, etc.). (see múrì, mútà).
(Sp. mirasol) The sunflower.
Useless, good-for-nothing, worthless, of little or no value, of no use, no good, of no value, base; small things, trifles. (see gadóy, walâ, sing-pulús, -águd, -ásoy, -átsoy, pitsépítse, karintukáy).
(B) See milôk-eyelash.
(Sp. miron) An onlooker, spectator, bystander, gazer.
(Sp.) A solemn Mass in which the celebrant is assisted by a deacon and subdeacon.
(Sp.) A solemn Mass in which the celebrant is assisted by a deacon and subdeacon.
(Sp.) A solemn Mass in which the celebrant is assisted by a deacon and subdeacon.
Altar; chapel, where Mass is said. (see halarán).
(Sp. misal) Missal, Mass-book.
(Sp. misterio) Mystery. (see katingaláhan, katanhagáan).
(Sp. místico) Mystical, mystic; spiritual.
(Sp. misticismo) Mysticism.
A kind of Chinese vermicelli, but finer than sutánghon.
(Sp. mision) Mission.
(Sp. misionero) Missionary.
Indigenous, native, not foreign or exotic. (see tumándok).
(English: meeting) Meeting, assembly, convention, caucus, a gathering or assemblage of people for some social or political purpose. (see tinipón-típon, katipúnan, katilíngban, hinubónhúbon).
(Sp. mitra) Mitre; bishop; episcopal curia.
(Sp. mecha) Fuse, match, match-cord, spark or flame used to fire gunpowder or fuel.
A kind of game at cards.
Your, yours, thy, thine, of you, of yours (singular); by or through you (thee). (see ímo, nímo and see ákon).
(Sp. moda) Mode, style, fashion, form, cut, shape, custom, manner, vogue. (see batásan, pamatásan, kinaanáran, úso, kinabatásan, kostúmbre).
(Sp. modelo) Model, pattern, standard, paragon, type, copy to be followed or imitated. (see huluáran, solóndan, palanganináwan).

To crush, pulverize, grind, pound or bray (in a mortar), crumble, powder; reduce to powder, comminute, triturate, break into fine particles by pressure; to become crushed or broken into small pieces. Modmorá ang karamélo, ang píghol, etc. Crush the caramel, the lump of rice, etc. Namódmod ang biskótso tungúd sang lumpálúmpa sang trak. The biscuits got crumbled owing to the jolting of the truck. Minódmod nga tinápay, kalámay, bugás, etc. Crumbled bread, powdered sugar, ground rice, etc. (see múdmud, bókbok, pódpod).

To blame, lay the blame on, impute, charge with, incriminate, censure, accuse, make responsible for, throw the guilt upon, find fault with, inculpate. Ginmokmokán siá níla sang mga kalaínan nga ginhímò sang ibán. He was made to answer for the wrong-doings of others, he was blamed by them for the evil done by others. Indì ka magmókmok sa íya sinâ. Don't lay the blame for that on him. Imókmok inâ sa may kalabtánan sinâ. Lay the blame for it on those involved in the affair. (see múkmuk id.).
(Sp. molde) Mould, pattern, form, block.

(Sp. moler) To grind, pound, crush, mill, pulverize, vex, molest, annoy, harass, bother, overwork. Nagmolér gid siá sa ákon. He annoyed me very much. (see galíng, galít, pasáklaw, huól, hiól, paugút).
Taciturn, silent, reticent, dumb, mum, uncommunicative, mute, close, not given to talking, not very sociable, of few words. (see komód).
To squeeze, push or press against, as one's head against a wall or floor, etc. (see nônô, sôsô, núsnus, uríud, oróod).

(B) An exclamation often placed at the end of a sentence; really, surely, certainly, indeed, believe me, etc. Indì akó magkádto dídto, mong. I am not going there, really I am not. Dakû siá, mong. He is a big fellow, sure enough.
A kind of peas, much eaten in the Philippines.

To cover, fill with alluvial matter. Ang dakû nga búhò dirâ sa ubús sang bakólod namonmonán tungúd sang madámol nga ulán. The large hole there at the foot of the hill was filled with alluvium due to the heavy rain. (see láy-on, punô, támpok, táp-ok).
(Sp. mono) Monkey, ape. (see amô).

To say, make a statement, state, declare, manifest, communicate, mention, utter, give out, make known, remark, drop a word. Si Pédro nagmóno nga mapatíndog sing bág-o nga baláy. Peter said that he was going to build a new house. Imóno sa íya ang kilidanón sang digamohán. Tell him about the necessary kitchen repairs. Ginmóno níya nga--. He gave out the statement that--. (see silíng, mítlang, bungát).
(Sp. monte) Mountain, forest, wood, woodland; a game at cards. Gindakúp silá sang polís, kay naghámpang sang mónte. They were caught by the police, because they were playing monte.
(Sp. monumento) Monument. (see batungdáan).
(Sp. muñeca) Doll, manikin, puppet, dolly.
To be deep, profound, heavy, sound, lethargic (of sleep). Nagamóok ang íya katulúgon. He is sleeping profoundly. Namoókan siá sang katulúgon. He was fast-, sound-, dead-, asleep. (see hamóok).
(Sp. morado) Violet, purple; brown, dark-red, mulberry-coloured, claret-coloured.
A kind of banana. It is very savoury and can easily be recognized by its brownish or reddish peel.
(Sp. moreno) Brown, swarthy, dark, tawny, brunette.
(Sp. morera) White mulberry tree.
(Sp. morisqueta) Boiled rice. (see kán-on).
To stammer, stutter, splutter, talk indistinctly through fear, shyness, etc.
Shirt. See kamísa tsína, kamísa de tsíno id.
See móro-Moor.
(Sp. mortal) Mortal, deadly, deathly, grievous, fatal. Salâ nga mortál. A mortal (grievous, deadly) sin. (see ikamatáy, kalamátyan).
See múrto-a ghost, etc.
(Sp. mosquitero) Mosquito-net or-curtain or-bar.
(Sp. mosquito) Mosquito, gnat. (see namók, lamók).
(Sp. muscovado) Unrefined sugar, muscovado.
(Sp. moton) Block, pulley. (see batakán).
(Sp. motor) Motor; dynamo.
Term of endearment for a pet monkey. (see amô).
A kind of ghost or spirit believed in by the superstitious. (see múwà id.).
To increase, multiply, propagate, breed, teem, procreate, have offspring. Nagmúad na gid iníng panimaláy. This family has increased very much. (see búad, pamúad).
To have one's mouth full or crammed with food, chew or speak with difficulty on account of having one's mouth stuffed with food, mutter, mumble, splutter.
See móda-fashion, etc.
To disparage, speak ill of, vilify, mock, scoff, insult, affront. Dakû ang íla pagmúda sa íya. They vilified (mocked, insulted) him very much. (see híkay, múlay, úmpit, ulígyat, uligâ).
To stare with greedy eyes, to gloat. See mulúdlò.
(Sp. mueble) Chattels, household goods, furniture, movables, outfit, equipment. (see galamitón, kasangkápan, sángkap).
(Sp. muelle) Pier, landing-stage, quay, jetty, wharf, mole; spring (of steel, rubber, etc.). (see pantalán).
(Sp. muerto) Dead, killed, deceased, departed, defunct; lifeless; corpse; ghost, spectre. (see múrto, patáy, minatáy, amalánhig).

To exert oneself, do something with force or violence. Nagmúg-ot siá sa paghákwat siníng bató. He put forth all his strength in lifting this stone. It was all he could do to lift this stone. Nagamúg-ot siá sa kaákig. He is violently angry. Ginmug-otán níya ang aparadór sa paggíhit. He made a great effort to shift the cupboard. Indì mo pagmug-otán ang ímo anák sang ákig. Don't be furiously angry with your son. (see paningúhà, panikasúg, himúd-os).
The rice-flower; pollen; to bloom or flower (of rice). (see marô).
(B) Short. See bugô, malíp-ot.

To get angry, exasperated, provoked, riled, indignant, cross, wax hot with anger. Nagamúgut na ang ginháwa ni Fuláno. N.N. is waxing hot, is getting angry or exasperated. Nagamúgut siá sa ákon. Ginamugútan (Ginamúgtan) níya akó. He is angry with me. (see ugút, ákig, sáklaw).
To be full, crammed, stuffed. Kon nagamúka ang ímo bâbâ índì ka maghámbal. Don't talk with a full mouth. (see punô, butâ, bát-al, báknal).
To lift or raise one's head. See tukháyaw, tukyáhaw.
To recover slightly, mend, rally, get a little better, improve. Nagmuk-háyaw na siá sa butí. He has now slightly recovered from the smallpox. (see mulikáw).

(H) To open (the eyes). Muklatá ang ímo mga matá. Open your eyes. Muklatí siá sang ímo mga matá. Look at him with open eyes. Mamúklat gid kunína ang íla mga matá. After some time they will have their eyes opened i.e. they will understand.
To blame for, etc. See mókmok id.
(B) See múklat.
(Sp. mula,-o) Mule, especially a she-mule; used also loosely of a large horse.
To look or stare at, notice with astonishment, be surprised to see, stare open-mouthed. (see pamalúng).
To strive, be active, do one's best, make great efforts. (see panikasúg, paningúhà, múg-ot).
Fist; to form, shape, fashion, handle (with one's fist). (see ómol).
To complain, show displeasure or discontent, lament, murmur, find fault with, grumble. (see kósmod, kúmud, pasingít, híkay, múlay).

(Sp. multa) Fine, mulct, extra payment, extra charge, pecuniary penalty; to fine, mulct, charge extra. Magmúlta ka sa íya or multahí siá sing tátlo ka mángmang. Fine him three pesos. Magbáyad ka lang sang múlta. Just pay the fine. (see tabís).
The East, sunrise, rising of the sun, Orient. (see murá, sidlangán).

To stare at with goggling or greedy eyes, gloat, devour with one's eyes. Nagamulúdlò ang íya mga matá sa kahákug. He is staring about with greedy eyes. His eyes are starting from his head. (see búdlò, múdlò, búslo).
Report, rumour, statement, information, news; to report, inform, give out a statement or news. (see múno).
See mútmut. Walâ makamulútmut ang íya nga hándum. His wish remained unfulfilled (literally:-was not without opposition-was thwarted).

A crumb, remains or leavings of food, especially a wasted grain of (cooked) rice. Ihátag na lang sa idô ang mga múmho nga nabilín sa látok. Give the leavings remaining on the table to the dog. (see míga).
Very ugly, shabby, mean, nasty and wicked like a monkey or even like an evil spirit. (see sárot).
To prosper, go on well, be well off, be well-to-do, be in good-, easy-, comfortable-, circumstances. (see kaayohán, mulumún-ag, tín-ad, manwáhà, úswag, sányog).
(Sp. mondo) Simple, timid, shy, bashful, unsophisticated; fool, ass, rustic, boorish, uneducated. (see bunáyag, antolô, bukídnon, manól, umánhon, kagúng, pákok, búngaw).
(Sp. mundo) World, orb, globe, earth. (see kalibútan, dútà),
A kind of banana.

A passive form (perhaps a contraction of manúng-an from panungâ, tungâ) often used in the meaning: to be hit-well,-full,-fairly,-right,-straight,-in the middle,-in the centre,-with full force; to be affected-, feel-, very much.
